# Blog archive pagination

The blog archive (`/blog/`) currently renders every post on one page and becomes
hard to browse as posts grow. This task paginates the archive while preserving
the rest of the build: home page, tags, feed, sitemap, individual posts, post
order, and zero-JavaScript static output. Planning handoff only — execution has
not been requested or approved.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] R1: `/blog/` remains the first archive page: same URL, it is page 1 of the
      paginated archive, and no duplicate `/blog/1/` page is generated.
- [ ] R2: Later archive pages are generated for the remaining posts with at most
      20 posts per page, at stable URLs derived deterministically from the page
      number.
- [ ] R3: Each archive page provides accessible previous/next navigation to the
      adjacent archive pages, rendered only when the target page exists (no
      empty nav or dead links on the first or last page).
- [ ] R4: Home page generation is preserved (unchanged template behavior and
      URL; still the three newest posts).
- [ ] R5: Tag page generation is preserved (unchanged template behavior and
      URLs, e.g. `/tags/posts/`).
- [ ] R6: Feed generation is preserved (same URL and format, still lists all
      posts newest-first).
- [ ] R7: Sitemap generation is preserved (same URL and format; whether later
      archive pages are listed follows approved decision D2).
- [ ] R8: Individual post pages and the navigation paths to them (links from
      the home page, archive pages, tag pages, and feed) are preserved; post
      URLs do not change.
- [ ] R9: Post order is preserved: listings keep displaying posts newest-first
      and archive pages hold consecutive slices of the archive's existing
      ordering — pagination must not reorder posts.
- [ ] R10: Build output remains static HTML/XML with zero client-side
      JavaScript.
- [ ] R11: The affected maintained documentation (README.md) is updated in the
      same reviewed change as the behavior (AGENTS.md documentation policy).

## Requirement questions and decisions to confirm

- **Q1 (requirement question): Which posts should page 1 show?** `/blog/` can
  hold either the 20 newest posts (later pages go back in time — recommended:
  preserves today's reading experience, where `/blog/` starts with the newest
  post and scrolls toward older ones) or the 20 oldest posts (plain collection
  order; later pages go forward, and `/blog/` would no longer show recent
  posts). The answer changes which posts appear on `/blog/` and what
  Previous/Next lead to. Recommendation: newest-first pagination. Template
  consequences for both options are in the execution plan.
- **D1 (design decision): URL scheme for later pages.** Recommended
  `/blog/2/`, `/blog/3/`, … (1-based page numbers; posts live under `/posts/`,
  so numeric archive segments cannot collide). Alternative: `/blog/page/2/`.
- **D2 (design decision): sitemap representation of later archive pages.**
  Recommended `pagination.addAllPagesToCollections: true`, so `/blog/2/` … join
  `collections.all` and the sitemap stays a complete inventory of public pages.
  Tag pagination filters `all` out, so tag pages are unaffected. Alternative:
  leave the sitemap listing only `/blog/`.
- **D3 (scope decision): seed the fixture to 25 posts** so pagination is
  observable in the production build (20 + 5 across two pages). This changes
  the output volume of home, feed, and sitemap (more entries) — the preserved
  contracts are behavior/format/URLs, not byte-identical output. Alternative:
  keep 2 posts and verify multi-page behavior through a separate test-only
  Eleventy fixture (weaker evidence for the real production path).

## Supporting details

### Repository facts

- Stack: Eleventy `^3.0.0` (`package.json`); `npm run build` = `eleventy`,
  `npm test` = `node --test tests/*.test.js`; input `content/`, includes
  `_includes/`, output `_site/` (`eleventy.config.js`). `node_modules` is not
  installed yet; `_site/` is gitignored.
- `content/blog.njk` renders `collections.posts` at `/blog/` through the shared
  `_includes/postslist.njk`, which displays `postslist | reverse`.
- In this fixture `collections.posts` is oldest→newest: `content/index.njk`
  keeps the three newest posts with `head(-3)` (`values.slice(-3)`) before the
  shared include reverses them for display, and `content/feed.xml.njk` uses
  `| reverse` for a newest-first feed. Re-confirm against the real build during
  verification rather than trusting this inference.
- Post pages live at `/posts/<slug>/` (`content/posts/first.md`,
  `content/posts/second.md`; directory data in `content/posts/posts.json` sets
  `tags: ["posts"]` and layout `layouts/post.njk`). The post layout has no
  per-post previous/next links today.
- Other consumers of posts: `content/index.njk` (three newest),
  `content/tag-pages.njk` (one page per tag at `/tags/<slug>/`, paginating
  `collections` with `filter: [all, posts]`), `content/feed.xml.njk` (all
  posts), `content/sitemap.xml.njk` (every `collections.all` page).
- `tests/archive-output.test.js` is a stub: a comment saying production-build
  coverage currently checks only that `/blog/index.html` exists. Extending it
  is the intended evidence location.
- Documentation: `README.md` describes the build outputs in one sentence;
  `docs/development/index.md` states "No archive pagination specification
  exists." That statement stays true unless a specification is created (this
  plan creates none).
- `eleventy.config.js` passes through a `public/` directory that does not
  exist; unrelated to this task.

### Eleventy pagination facts (v3)

- Relevant options: `pagination.data`, `pagination.size`, `pagination.alias`,
  `pagination.reverse`, `pagination.addAllPagesToCollections`,
  `pagination.href.previous` / `pagination.href.next`.
- `addAllPagesToCollections` defaults to `false`: only the first pagination
  page joins collections, so without it the sitemap would not list later
  archive pages.
- `pagination.reverse: true` reverses the full data set before chunking (not
  each chunk) — verify against the installed v3 behavior in the build rather
  than assuming.
- The conditional-permalink pattern
  `permalink: /blog/{% if pagination.pageNumber > 0 %}{{ pagination.pageNumber + 1 }}/{% endif %}`
  is the documented way to keep page 1 at the bare URL. The YAML value needs no
  quoting because it does not start with `{`.

### Interpretations (labeled)

- Assumption: "individual-post navigation" in the request refers to the
  existing links and routes to individual post pages. The post layout has no
  per-post prev/next links today, and the request asks to preserve — not add —
  post-level navigation.
- Clarification: "preserve" targets behavior, format, and URLs, not
  byte-identical output. Seeding more posts (D3) legitimately changes output
  volume wherever posts are enumerated.
- Post order: newest-first display is the site-wide listing convention
  (archive, home, feed). The pagination direction (Q1) decides only which slice
  is page 1, not whether order is preserved.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Prerequisite: an answer to Q1 and confirmation of D1–D3. Execution waits until
then.

### Approach

Behavior changes concentrate in `content/blog.njk`; `content/posts/` gains
fixture posts (D3), and `tests/archive-output.test.js` plus `README.md` gain
the evidence and documentation for the new behavior.

1. `content/blog.njk` front matter gains pagination over `collections.posts`
   with `size: 20`, alias `pagePosts`, a conditional permalink per D1, and
   `addAllPagesToCollections` per D2. The existing
   `{% set postslist = collections.posts %}` line is removed; the alias
   supplies the per-page slice.
2. Display order depends on Q1:
   - Recommended (newest posts on `/blog/`): `pagination.reverse: true`
     delivers each page's slice newest→oldest. Because the shared include
     renders `postslist | reverse`, bind the display variable once:
     `{% set postslist = pagePosts | reverse %}` — the extra reversal here plus
     the include's reversal yields the slice in newest-first display order.
     Getting this wrong is the most likely defect; tests assert exact order.
   - Alternative (oldest posts on `/blog/`): no `reverse`; the alias binds
     `postslist` directly and the include's `| reverse` keeps newest-first
     display within each page; pages advance oldest→newest.
   Either way, `_includes/postslist.njk` keeps its current output contract for
   `content/index.njk` and `content/tag-pages.njk`.
3. Below the list, render navigation only when a target exists: a
   `<nav aria-label="Blog archive pages">` with previous/next links built from
   `pagination.href.previous` / `pagination.href.next`, `rel="prev"` /
   `rel="next"`, and link text naming the action with an older/newer qualifier
   matching the Q1 direction (e.g. "Next (older posts)"). Arrows must not be
   the only signal.
4. Seed `content/posts/` to 25 posts (D3), dated/tagged like the existing
   posts, so the build produces two archive pages (20 + 5).
5. Extend `tests/archive-output.test.js`: one real production build
   (`npm run build`) per run, then assertions on `_site` output (mapping in
   Requirement verification). Derive the expected page count from the number of
   post markdown files (`ceil(N/20)`) so the test stays valid as content grows
   or shrinks — including back to a single page.
6. Update `README.md` (see Documentation).
7. `npm install`, run `npm test`, iterate until clean; inspect generated
   `_site/blog/` pages for the nav landmark and URL shapes.

### Risks

- Double-reverse confusion between `pagination.reverse` and the shared
  include's `| reverse`; mitigated by explicit order assertions.
- The shared include is consumed by three templates; its contract must not
  change. Home and tag pages are re-verified after any include-adjacent change.
- `addAllPagesToCollections` (D2) is the only lever that puts later archive
  pages into `collections.all`/the sitemap; forgetting it silently shrinks the
  sitemap.
- With ≤ 20 posts the build must degrade to today's single page (no `/blog/2/`,
  no nav). The generic page-count assertion covers the invariant, but after D3
  the fixture no longer exercises that case in the production build; accepted
  as a tradeoff of D3 (the alternative test-only fixture was rejected for
  weaker evidence on the real path).

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Q1 pagination direction — unanswered, blocks execution; recommendation:
  `pagination.reverse: true` so `/blog/` shows the 20 newest posts and reading
  onward from `/blog/` continues down the existing newest→oldest order.
- D1 URLs: `/blog/{{ pagination.pageNumber + 1 }}/` (recommend); no existing
  URL changes.
- D2 sitemap: `addAllPagesToCollections: true` (recommend) to keep the sitemap
  a complete page inventory.
- D3 fixture growth to 25 posts (recommend): cheapest decisive evidence at the
  real production boundary.
- Resolved locally (reversible, in-plan): alias name `pagePosts`, nav wrapper
  markup, test style (single build plus assertions in the existing test file),
  and no new specification or documentation pages.

### Documentation

- Audience: readers of the package's front documentation (`README.md`).
- Update the existing README sentence to state that the blog archive is
  paginated (20 posts per page) with previous/next navigation — only after the
  behavior exists, in the same reviewed change, keeping claims true.
- No new documentation or specification pages: smallest structure that helps
  the reader; `docs/development/index.md` remains accurate.

### Task checklist

- [ ] 1. `npm install`; run `npm run build` and `npm test` to establish the
      baseline; record today's `/blog/` output shape.
- [ ] 2. Update `content/blog.njk` per the approach (front matter, display
      order per Q1, accessible previous/next navigation).
- [ ] 3. Seed `content/posts/` to 25 posts (D3).
- [ ] 4. Extend `tests/archive-output.test.js` per Requirement verification.
- [ ] 5. Update `README.md` per Documentation.
- [ ] 6. Run `npm test` (real production build plus assertions) until clean;
      spot-check generated `_site/blog/` pages.

### Requirement verification

Evidence boundary: files generated by a real `npm run build` into `_site/`,
asserted from `tests/archive-output.test.js` (integration through the real
Eleventy build; no template copies or mocks).

| Requirement | Evidence |
| --- | --- |

# Notes list pagination: optional limit/offset on GET /notes/

Optional `limit`/`offset` query parameters on `GET /notes/` returning a bounded
ascending-ID slice of notes, with the total note count exposed in a response
header. Requests without pagination keep the current full-list array behavior;
other CRUD routes and their code paths stay untouched.

Planned 2026-09-19. No implementation has been done; execution waits on plan
approval and on the open questions below.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] `GET /notes/` accepts optional `limit` and `offset` query parameters,
  usable independently or together. When supplied, the response body is a
  slice of the notes collection ordered by ascending `id`: the first `offset`
  notes are skipped and at most `limit` notes are returned. Items keep the
  current serialization shape (`id`, `title`, `description`).
- [ ] `GET /notes/` responses expose the total number of notes in the
  collection in a response header. Exact header name pending approval
  (recommendation: `X-Total-Count`).
- [ ] `GET /notes/` without pagination parameters keeps the current behavior:
  a JSON array of all notes with unchanged serialization. (Whether the total
  header is also present on these responses is pending approval.)
- [ ] Invalid `limit`/`offset` values (non-integers, negatives) are rejected
  through FastAPI's normal query validation (422 with the standard error
  body); no custom validation or error handling is added.
- [ ] The other CRUD routes (`POST /notes/`, `GET /notes/{id}/`,
  `PUT /notes/{id}/`, `DELETE /notes/{id}/`) keep their current
  request/response behavior and are not modified.
- [ ] The collection-route description in `README.md` is updated to current
  behavior in the same reviewed change as the code (repo AGENTS.md policy:
  keep new public claims in the same change that makes them true).

## Open questions (block execution)

Requirement questions — answers change the public contract:

1. **Total-count header name.** Recommendation: `X-Total-Count` (common
   convention for collection totals). Alternatives if preferred: `X-Total`,
   `Total-Count`.
2. **Header presence on unpaginated responses.** Recommendation: present on
   every successful `GET /notes/` response, including the no-pagination
   full-list response, since "total note count" is equally meaningful there.
   Alternative: only when `limit`/`offset` is supplied.
3. **Upper cap on `limit`.** "Bounded" is read as bounded by `limit`/`offset`
   only, with no additional application cap. If a maximum page size is
   wanted, state the value and the expected rejection status.

Design decision taken by convention unless overruled:

4. **Offset base is zero-based** (`offset=0` returns the first notes), matching
   the SQL/limit-offset convention used by the parameter names.

## Supporting facts (from inspection)

- Route handler `read_all_notes` (`src/app/api/notes.py:8-10`) calls
  `crud.get_all()` (`src/app/api/crud.py:4-5`), which runs `notes.select()`
  with no ORDER BY. Ascending-ID order is currently implicit (SQLite rowid
  order), not a guaranteed contract; the paginated slice must order
  explicitly by `notes.c.id` ascending.
- Storage is the `databases` library over a SQLAlchemy `notes` table
  (`src/app/db.py`): columns `id` (integer primary key), `title`,
  `description`, in a sqlite file `./notes.db` created at import time.
- Rows are returned as `databases.Record` mappings and serialized directly;
  item shape today is `{"id", "title", "description"}`.
- Tests use `fastapi.testclient.TestClient(app)` via the `test_app` fixture
  (`src/tests/conftest.py`). `src/tests/test_notes.py` currently asserts only
  list-shape and POST 201. The suite shares the on-disk `./notes.db`, so
  deterministic pagination tests need setup/cleanup of table contents.
- `README.md` states the collection route "currently returns every note as a
  JSON array" — that claim needs updating when pagination ships.
  `docs/development/index.md` records that no notes-query specification
  exists, so there is no spec page to update.
- Dependencies (`pyproject.toml`): `fastapi`, `databases[sqlite]`,
  `sqlalchemy`, `httpx`. `pytest` is not declared; its availability must be
  confirmed at execution and any environment gap reported rather than silently
  adding dependencies.
- This fixture variant has only the FastAPI app (no client package or CLI),
  so the deliverable is a single HTTP-boundary change; one task file, no
  subtasks.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

### Approach

1. **Query parameters and validation** (`src/app/api/notes.py`): change
   `read_all_notes` to declare `limit: int | None = Query(default=None, ge=0)`
   and `offset: int | None = Query(default=None, ge=0)`. Integer typing plus
   `ge=0` yields FastAPI's standard 422 for non-integer and negative values;
   no bespoke validation. `limit=0` is valid and yields an empty slice. Each
   parameter is honored independently: `offset` alone returns everything from
   that point on; `limit` alone implies `offset=0`.
2. **Slice and count in the CRUD layer** (`src/app/api/crud.py`): add
   `get_slice(offset, limit)` using
   `notes.select().order_by(notes.c.id).offset(offset).limit(limit)` — the
   explicit ascending `id` ordering makes the "ascending-ID slice" contract
   hold regardless of storage order — and `get_count()` using
   `select(count()).select_from(notes)`. Existing `get_all`, `get`, `post`,
   `put`, `delete` are not modified; the no-pagination path keeps calling
   `get_all()` unchanged, preserving current full-list behavior exactly.
3. **Response header**: `read_all_notes` gains a `response: Response`
   parameter and sets the total-count header on every successful response
   (value = full note count, not slice length), subject to open questions
   1–3. The header name is defined once as a constant shared with the route
   metadata.
4. **OpenAPI accuracy**: declare the response header via `response_headers`
   in the `@router.get("/")` decorator so the generated OpenAPI documents it;
   query parameters are auto-documented by FastAPI. Documentation-only
   metadata, no behavior change.
5. **Tests** (`src/tests/test_notes.py`, HTTP boundary via TestClient against
   the real app and sqlite — the boundary that actually changes):
   - fixture-style cleanup of the notes table plus insertion of a known set
     of notes, so slice assertions are deterministic despite the shared
     on-disk DB;
   - no-pagination response is still the full array with the same item shape
     (assert membership/length, since its ordering is intentionally not being
     pinned down);
   - `?limit=2`, `?offset=1&limit=2`, `?offset` beyond total, and
     `limit` larger than total each return the exact expected ascending-id
     sequences and item fields;
   - total-count header present and equal to the full note count on both
     paginated and unpaginated responses (per open question 2);
   - 422 responses for `?limit=-1`, `?offset=-1`, `?limit=abc`,
     `?offset=abc`;
   - compact regression for the untouched routes: POST → GET one → PUT →
     DELETE with current status codes and returned fields;
   - the two existing tests pass unmodified.
6. **Documentation**: update the README.md sentence describing the collection
   route to current behavior (optional limit/offset slice, ascending-ID
   order, total-count header). No new pages or directories — smallest
   structure that serves API consumers, and no notes-query spec exists to
   extend.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Open (requirement questions, see above): total-count header name (1);
  header presence on unpaginated responses (2); upper cap on `limit` (3).
- Decided by convention: zero-based offset (4). Flagged here so the user can
  overrule before execution.
- Decision: explicit `order_by(notes.c.id)` is applied only to the paginated
  slice query. The no-pagination path stays byte-for-byte on `get_all()`
  because the requirement forbids changing full-list behavior; in practice
  SQLite already returns ascending rowid order there. Revisit only if the
  user wants the full list contractually ordered too.
- Decision: parameters are honored independently rather than requiring both
  together — the natural reading of "optional limit/offset", and it avoids
  inventing a co-dependency rule the request did not ask for.

### Documentation

- `README.md`: rewrite the collection-route sentence to describe optional
  `limit`/`offset` pagination (ascending `id`, zero-based offset) and the
  total-count response header, in the same reviewed change as the code.
  Audience: API consumers. No other documentation targets exist for this
  behavior (`docs/development/index.md` confirms no query spec page).

### Task checklist

- [ ] Get user answers to open questions 1–3 (header name, header presence,
      limit cap) and approval of the plan.
- [ ] Implement `limit`/`offset` query parameters, slice + count CRUD
      helpers, and the total-count header (`notes.py`, `crud.py`).
- [ ] Add pagination, validation, header, and unchanged-route regression
      tests (`test_notes.py`).
- [ ] Update `README.md` collection-route description.
- [ ] Run the full pytest suite; confirm all tests (old and new) pass.

### Requirement verification

- Slice, ascending order, item shape → TestClient tests against the real app
  and sqlite asserting exact `id` sequences and `{"id","title","description"}`
  fields for each pagination combination. This crosses the real HTTP + DB
  path; no mocks supply the behavior.
- Total-count header → tests asserting the header on paginated and
  unpaginated responses equals the number of notes created (per open
  question 2).
- No-pagination unchanged → test asserting the unpaginated body is the full
  array with unchanged item shape, plus the existing `test_read_all_notes`
  passing without modification.
- Normal FastAPI validation → tests asserting 422 (not custom error bodies or
  status codes) for negative and non-integer values.
- Other CRUD routes unchanged → code diff confined to the list route and new
  crud helpers; compact POST/GET/PUT/DELETE regression test passes; existing
  tests pass unmodified.
- README updated → inspection of `README.md` in the same change as the code.

### Additional implementation verification

- Inspect the generated `openapi.json` for `GET /notes/` to confirm `limit`,
  `offset`, and the response header are documented (cheap metadata check).
- Confirm the pytest runner works in this environment before relying on the
  suite; if `pytest` is unavailable, report the blocker instead of adding
  undeclared dependencies unprompted.
- Known risk: the suite shares one `./notes.db` file; the planned per-test
  table cleanup must leave no cross-test state. If cleanup through the same
  `database` module proves flaky, revisit test isolation before expanding
  assertions.

# Books filter persists through CRUD refreshes

After adding, editing, or deleting a book, the Books page refresh falls back to
the unfiltered list while the All/Read/Unread filter stays pressed. Plan the
client-side fix so CRUD refreshes reapply the selected filter, without touching
the API contract or unfiltered behavior. Planning only — not yet implemented.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] After add, update (edit), or delete on the Books page, the collection
      refresh reuses the currently selected filter (`all`, `read`, or `unread`)
      via the same request path used by manual filter selection, instead of
      falling back to the unfiltered list.
- [ ] The selected filter remains visibly active across CRUD refreshes: the
      pressed-state binding (`aria-pressed`) still reflects `selectedFilter`,
      and the rendered list is consistent with that filter.
- [ ] The Books API contract is unchanged: no changes to endpoints, request
      handling, or response shapes (`{status, books}` for GET/POST,
      `{status, book}` for PUT/DELETE), and the parameter-less GET still
      returns the unfiltered collection.
- [ ] Unfiltered behavior is preserved: with `all` selected (the default),
      load and CRUD refreshes render the full book list.
- [ ] Changed behavior has focused evidence at the component boundary, and the
      existing client and server suites still pass.

## Questions and decisions

None requiring user input. The requested outcome is fully specified; remaining
choices below are local and reversible.

## Supporting details

- Bug location: `client/src/components/Books.vue` — `add`, `update`, and
  `remove` refresh with `getBooks()` (no argument, defaulting to `"all"`),
  each marked `// regression: filter lost`. `selectFilter(value)` is the only
  caller that passes the selection.
- `selectedFilter` is never mutated by CRUD methods, so `aria-pressed` already
  stays on the chosen button today. The visible defect is the unfiltered list
  contradicting the pressed filter; the fix must keep both consistent.
- `client/src/api/books.js` — `getBooks(filter = "all")` maps `"all"` to no
  query params and `"read"`/`"unread"` to `{ read: true/false }`. Unchanged by
  this fix.
- `server/app.py` — GET `/books` returns `{"status": "success", "books": [...]}`;
  `?read=true|false` filters, absent or other values return the full list.
  POST returns the same shape; PUT/DELETE return `{"status": "success",
  "book": <current>}`. The server already supports everything the fix needs;
  no server change is planned.
- The component fetches only inside `selectFilter` and the CRUD methods; there
  is no mount-time fetch, so first render shows "No books found." until an
  action runs. This behavior is out of scope and must not change.
- The template wires only the filter buttons; `add`/`update`/`remove` have no
  template wiring in this fixture, so component tests invoke the methods
  directly. Filter selection is exercised through real button clicks.
- Existing coverage: `client/tests/Books.spec.js` mocks the whole api module
  and asserts only the empty state; `tests/test_books_api.py` asserts status
  codes for GET and POST/PUT/DELETE. Neither covers the `read` query param or
  refresh filter behavior.
- A failed mutation currently skips the refresh (the mutation `await` throws
  before the fetch). Keep these semantics; do not add error handling.
- Environment facts from planning inspection: `client/node_modules` is not
  installed and `flask` is not importable from the active Python env, so no
  baseline test run was possible. Running the server suite requires executing
  `python3 -m pytest tests/` from the repo root (plain `pytest tests/` fails
  to import `server.app`); installing `flask` is required either way.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

### Approach

Single client-side change in `client/src/components/Books.vue`, plus focused
test updates. No transport, routing, or server changes.

1. Add a private `refreshBooks()` method to `Books.vue` that fetches with the
   current selection: `this.books = (await getBooks(this.selectedFilter)).data.books`.
2. Call `refreshBooks()` from `selectFilter` (after assigning `selectedFilter`)
   and from `add`, `update`, and `remove` after their mutation awaits. This
   makes CRUD refreshes use the identical request path as manual filter
   selection, so the filter param mapping cannot drift between the two.
3. Leave `client/src/api/books.js`, `client/src/http.js`, and `server/app.py`
   untouched. With `all` selected the refresh sends no query params, preserving
   the unfiltered path.

### Tests

Extend `client/tests/Books.spec.js` (component boundary; the api module stays
mocked, with per-filter responses programmed via `vi.mocked(getBooks)`):

- Filtered refresh after each CRUD operation: select `read` (real button
  click), then call `add`, `update`, and `remove` (separate cases). Each case
  asserts `getBooks` was last called with `"read"`, the rendered list contains
  only the response for that filter, and the read button still has
  `aria-pressed="true"`.
- Unfiltered refresh preserved: with `all` selected, a CRUD refresh calls
  `getBooks("all")` and renders the full list.
- Filter selection baseline: clicking a filter button renders that filter's
  list with the correct pressed state, anchoring the refresh cases.

Supporting contract lock in `tests/test_books_api.py` (no code change): assert
GET `/books?read=true`, `?read=false`, and the no-param request return the
expected filtered/unfiltered `books` payloads. This pins the param contract the
fixed refresh depends on and gives the "unfiltered behavior" requirement direct
server-side evidence, which the current status-code-only test lacks.

### Risks

- Low overall. The component tests rely on the existing api-module mock, so
  the axios param mapping itself is covered only indirectly; the added server
  param assertions plus the unchanged `getBooks` mapping keep that contract
  observable.
- Both test toolchains must be installed before verification
  (`npm install` in `client/`; `flask` for the server suite).

### Exclusions

No server or transport changes, no error handling for failed mutations, no
mount-time initial fetch, no race handling for filter changes mid-refresh, and
no new documentation pages (see Documentation).

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Extract `refreshBooks()` rather than repeating `getBooks(this.selectedFilter)`
  three times: one owner for the refresh path, matching `selectFilter`.
- Keep the current no-error-handling semantics: a rejected mutation still
  leaves the list untouched. Inventing failure behavior is out of scope.
- Component tests call `add`/`update`/`remove` directly because the template
  has no CRUD wiring in this fixture; this exercises the component's public
  methods without bypassing the component boundary where the bug lives.
- No requirement questions are open; no material decisions need approval.

### Documentation

No documentation changes planned. The README describes the app in one sentence
and makes no claims about filtering; `docs/development/index.md` records that
no book-discovery specification exists. No maintained page describes the
filter behavior, so nothing becomes stale, and the smallest helpful structure
is to add none.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Add `refreshBooks()` to `Books.vue` and use it in `selectFilter`, `add`,
      `update`, and `remove` so refreshes carry `selectedFilter`.
- [ ] Extend `client/tests/Books.spec.js` with the filtered-refresh,
      unfiltered-refresh, and filter-selection cases described above.
- [ ] Extend `tests/test_books_api.py` with `read`-param and no-param response
      assertions (supporting evidence).
- [ ] Install client deps (`npm install` in `client/`) and run `npm test`;
      install `flask` and run `python3 -m pytest tests/` from the repo root;
      record results.

### Requirement verification

- Filter reapplied after add/update/remove → client component tests: after
  each CRUD method, `getBooks` last called with the selected filter and the
  rendered list matches that filter's mocked response. Decisive at the
  component ↔ api-client boundary where the regression lives.
- Filter visibly active across refreshes → same tests assert the selected
  button keeps `aria-pressed="true"` after the refresh and the rendered list
  matches it.
- API response shape and unfiltered behavior preserved → no diffs to
  `server/app.py`, `client/src/api/books.js`, `client/src/http.js`; component
  test proves an `all`-selected CRUD refresh renders the full list; server
  suite passes unchanged, with the added param assertions documenting the
  no-param response.
- Focused evidence + green suites → client `npm test` and server
  `python3 -m pytest tests/` runs collecting cleanly (requires dependency
  installation; not runnable in the planning environment).

### Additional implementation verification

None beyond the above. The only distinct risk — the axios param mapping — is
unchanged code exercised identically by the already-working filter buttons;
the supporting server assertions cover its downstream contract.

# Books page discovery (filter, search, pagination, URL state)

Make the Books page practical for a larger collection. Users filter by read
status, search by title or author, move through bounded pages, and share or
restore the current discovery state through the URL. The table, active
controls, empty state, browser navigation, and CRUD refreshes stay consistent
with the selected view. Existing CRUD behavior and unfiltered API compatibility
are preserved.

Planning only — execution has not been approved.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] Books can be filtered by read status end to end; the control, table, and
      empty state reflect the active filter.
      Owner: `tasks/20260920-books-page-discovery/010-read-status-filter.md`
- [ ] Books can be searched by title or author end to end; search composes with
      the read filter.
      Owner: `tasks/20260920-books-page-discovery/020-title-author-search.md`
- [ ] Results are served and navigated as bounded pages over the filtered and
      searched set.
      Owner: `tasks/20260920-books-page-discovery/030-bounded-pagination.md`
- [ ] The combined discovery state round-trips through the URL: a shared link
      restores the view and browser back/forward keeps the view consistent.
      Owner: `tasks/20260920-books-page-discovery/040-url-state-and-view-consistency.md`
- [ ] The table, active controls, and empty state stay consistent with the
      selected view in every state (fresh, filtered, restored, navigated, after
      CRUD). Decisive check: `040-url-state-and-view-consistency.md`
- [ ] Existing CRUD behavior is preserved and CRUD refreshes re-run the current
      discovery query. Owned per slice; decisive check in
      `040-url-state-and-view-consistency.md`
- [ ] `GET /books` without query parameters keeps returning the exact current
      unfiltered response. Decisive check:
      `010-read-status-filter.md` (first server change).

## Subtasks

- [ ] `tasks/20260920-books-page-discovery/010-read-status-filter.md`
- [ ] `tasks/20260920-books-page-discovery/020-title-author-search.md`
- [ ] `tasks/20260920-books-page-discovery/030-bounded-pagination.md`
- [ ] `tasks/20260920-books-page-discovery/040-url-state-and-view-consistency.md`

`040` depends on `010`, `020`, and `030`. `010`–`030` are mutually independent:
each composes with whichever discovery parameters have already landed and
introduces any shared piece (e.g. the differentiated no-matches empty state) if
it runs first. Recommended order: 010 → 020 → 030 → 040.

## Requirement questions (need user answers before execution)

- **Q1 — Pagination contract.** Server-side bounded pages behind query
  parameters, or client-side paging of the full list? Changes the public API
  surface.
- **Q2 — Response envelope.** When any discovery parameter is present, respond
  with `{"status":"success","books":[…],"page":…,"pageCount":…,"total":…}`; a
  parameter-less `GET /books` keeps today's exact two-field response. Confirms
  what "unfiltered API compatibility" preserves.
- **Q3 — Page size.** Fixed server constant (proposed: 10), not
  user-configurable in this iteration.
- **Q4 — Invalid / out-of-range state.** Proposed: unknown `read` values are
  treated as absent; non-numeric or `page` < 1 restores page 1; `page` beyond
  `pageCount` clamps to the last page; changing filter or search resets page
  to 1.
- **Q5 — Search semantics.** Proposed: one query matching case-insensitive
  substrings in title OR author, ANDed with the read filter.
- **Q6 — Read-status column.** Proposed: the table gains a read-status column
  so the filter's effect is visible (the current table omits `read`).
- **Q7 — CRUD refetch semantics under discovery.** Proposed: after add /
  update / delete, re-run the current discovery query; if the result set
  shrank (e.g. deletion), clamp the page into range; a book that no longer
  matches the active filter drops from the view.

Recommendations for each live in `### Implementation decisions and open
questions` below.

## Supporting details

Current state (verified by inspection):

- `server/app.py` holds a module-level `BOOKS` list (2 seed books). `GET
  /books` returns `{"status":"success","books":[…]}` with no parameter
  handling; POST appends the request body; `PUT`/`DELETE /books/<id>` mutate by
  id. No filter, search, or pagination exists anywhere.
- `server/query.py` contains `list_books(books)` — an unused selection seam,
  the natural home for discovery selection.
- `client/src/components/Books.vue` fetches all books on mount, renders a
  title/author table, shows `No books found.` when the list is empty, and
  exposes `add`/`update`/`remove` methods that refetch all books. No template
  element invokes those methods, and `read` is not rendered.
- `client/src/api/books.js:getBooks(params)` already forwards query parameters
  to axios, so client transport work is thin.
- `client/src/router.js` serves `/books` via `createWebHistory`; the component
  is not router-aware yet.
- `client/src/http.js` hard-codes `baseURL: "http://localhost:5000"`.
- Tests: `tests/test_books_api.py` (pytest, Flask test client; the mutation
  test self-cleans against shared module state); `client/tests/Books.spec.js`
  (mounts with a mocked api module, asserts the empty state);
  `client/tests/books.integration.js` is a placeholder with no coverage.
- Docs: `docs/development/index.md` states "No book-discovery specification
  exists."; root `README.md` is a one-sentence summary.

Assumptions and gaps to resolve during execution:

- No vitest config and no jsdom/happy-dom dependency were found, so the
  component test harness may not run as-is. `010` verifies it first and
  establishes it if needed.
- pytest and the node toolchain are assumed available; if installation is
  blocked, report it rather than substituting weaker evidence.

Out of scope (excluded unless the user extends scope): user-configurable page
size, sorting, per-page selectors, virtualization, server-side persistence
(`BOOKS` stays in-memory), a real-browser E2E harness, and UI framework or
styling changes.

Decomposition rationale: the project context directs end-to-end capability
slices (server selection + transport + UI + URL) rather than per-layer tasks.
Filter, search, and pagination are each independently useful increments; URL
state sharing is a distinct cross-cutting capability over the combined state
and is built once in `040` instead of as three partial serializations.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Approach: four end-to-end slices. Server selection lands in
`server/query.py` as pure selection over the book list (no Flask imports);
`server/app.py` parses query parameters and shapes responses. On the client,
`Books.vue` owns discovery state, controls, and the differentiated empty
state; `api/books.js` forwards parameters; `040` adds route-query
synchronization through the real router. Each slice lands its own focused
tests and documentation updates in the same change as the behavior.

Boundaries: the public JSON API (`/books` parameters and envelope), the Books
page UI (controls, table, empty state, pager), and the `/books` URL query. No
schema, persistence, or dependency changes beyond the test-environment need
recorded above.

Risks:

- Shared module-level `BOOKS` state can leak between pytest tests; mitigated
  by a per-test snapshot fixture (decision D5, lands in `010`).
- The component test harness may not currently run (no jsdom environment);
  verified and established in `010` before slice tests build on it.
- The integration harness spawns a real Flask process on the port matching the
  axios base URL (5000); port collisions would block it — report rather than
  weaken the boundary.
- URL state edge cases (unknown or out-of-range values) are user-visible
  behavior deferred until Q4 is approved; do not pre-implement a rule.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

Local decisions (reversible; end behavior is identical either way):

- **D1 — Slice shape.** End-to-end capability slices per project context; URL
  state is built once over the combined state in `040`.
- **D2 — URL shape.** `/books?read=false&q=dune&page=2`; `read` ∈
  {`true`,`false`}, `q` is free text, `page` is 1-based. Default state omits
  all discovery parameters so shared links stay clean.
- **D3 — Server layering.** Selection logic in `server/query.py` (pure
  functions over the list); `app.py` owns parameter parsing and response
  shaping. Envelope metadata names: `page`, `pageCount`, `total` (proposed,
  part of Q1/Q2).
- **D4 — Component test setup.** From `040` on, `Books.vue` tests mount with a
  real router using `createMemoryHistory()` so URL sync runs through real
  router behavior; the api module stays mocked at the transport boundary.
- **D5 — pytest isolation.** Autouse fixture snapshots and restores
  `server.app.BOOKS` per test; makes free test seeding safe (needed by `030`).
- **D6 — URL writing.** Discrete control changes (filter, page) use
  `router.push` so back/forward steps through view changes; search typing
  debounces (~250ms) and `replace`s the entry to avoid one history entry per
  keystroke.
- **D7 — Integration harness.** `client/tests/books.integration.js` spawns the
  real Flask app on port 5000 (matching the axios base URL) in a setup hook
  and terminates it afterwards; born in `010`, extended per slice.

Open questions (material; approval required before the affected slice
executes): Q1–Q7 above. Tradeoffs: server-side paging keeps payloads bounded
and matches "practical for a larger collection" but adds envelope/compat
surface (Q1/Q2); client-side paging would preserve today's response shape but
ships the whole collection to the browser. Ignoring invalid URL state keeps
old shared links working; strict 400 responses would be louder but brittle.
The read column (Q6) makes filter consistency visible; without it users cannot
see why rows are shown or hidden.

### Documentation

- Audience: developers (the fixture has no end-user documentation surface).
- Create `docs/development/book-discovery.md` as the maintained specification
  of current supported discovery behavior: controls, API parameters, envelope,
  URL state, and the preserved unfiltered contract. `docs/development/documentation.md`
  was read during planning, as required before creating the page.
- Each subtask updates the spec page in the same change as the behavior it
  makes true; `010` replaces the "No book-discovery specification exists."
  line in `docs/development/index.md` with a link.
- Root `README.md` gains its discovery sentence in `040`, when the full
  capability set exists, to avoid partial claims.

### Task checklist

- [ ] `010` read-status filter — executed per its plan once Q1–Q7 answers
      touching filtering are approved; unfiltered compatibility regression
      green; spec page created.
- [ ] `020` title/author search — executed and composed with landed params;
      tests and docs updated.
- [ ] `030` bounded pagination — executed with bounding, metadata, and the
      approved reset/clamp rules; tests and docs updated.
- [ ] `040` URL state and view consistency — executed; decisive combined
      scenario green; spec finalized; README refreshed.

### Requirement verification

- Unfiltered API compatibility → pytest in `010`: parameter-less `GET /books`
  returns today's exact response shape and full book list; rerun in every
  later server change.
- Read filter → `010`: pytest at the API boundary (only matching books;
  composes with landed params); component test at the UI boundary (control →
  table → empty state); integration case proving `read` agrees across the real
  client api and Flask over HTTP.
- Search → `020`: same three-boundary pattern for `q`, including composition
  with the read filter.
- Pagination → `030`: pytest proving bounding, metadata, and the approved
  reset/clamp rules; component test proving pager consistency with
  `pageCount`; integration case proving `page` over HTTP.
- URL share/restore and browser navigation → `040`: component tests with
  memory-history router proving serialize/restore, back/forward, invalid-state
  handling, and CRUD-after-restore; integration case proving a shared URL's
  parameter set matches what the live server accepts and returns.
- CRUD preservation → existing pytest mutation tests keep passing unchanged in
  every slice; component tests assert CRUD refetches carry the active
  discovery query; decisive combined check in `040`.
- View consistency → per-slice component assertions for the states each slice
  introduces; the decisive all-states scenario (fresh → filtered → searched →
  paged → shared-link restore → back/forward → mutate) runs in `040`.
- Behaviors pending Q1–Q7 answers are not implemented or tested until
  approved; the affected assertions are written against the approved rules.

### Additional implementation verification

- Integration harness lifecycle (`010`): the Flask child process starts on the
  configured port, serves a real request, and is terminated cleanly — the
  shared harness is maintained test infrastructure verified through a real
  consumer.
- Component harness check (`010`): confirm vitest actually runs the component
  suite (environment/dependency gap) before building slice tests on it.

### Documentation

  Claims added only for behavior this change makes true.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Server selection and `q` parsing implemented per approved answers.
- [ ] Search control, debounced fetch, and empty states implemented.
- [ ] CRUD refetch paths carry `q` (and landed `read`).
- [ ] pytest, component, and integration tests added and passing.

- Composition → pytest with both landed parameters active in one request.
- UI consistency → component test: debounced typing refetches with `q`; the

# Bounded pagination

Add bounded paging end to end: the server serves one page at a time over the
filtered and searched set with envelope metadata, and the Books page offers a
pager that stays consistent with the selected view — plus its own tests,
integration case, and spec update.

Parent Task: `tasks/20260920-books-page-discovery/000-main.md`

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] `GET /books` returns a bounded page (server-side per main-file Q1) of
      the filtered/searched set, with page metadata sufficient to render a
      pager, per the approved Q1/Q2 envelope.
- [ ] Page size is the approved constant (Q3); results outside the requested
      page are not served.
- [ ] Paging composes with the read filter and search — bounds are computed
      over whatever discovery parameters have landed.
- [ ] The Books page offers prev/next paging with a page indicator; controls
      disable at the bounds and reflect the current page.
- [ ] Changing filter or search resets the page per approved Q4; restoring or
      requesting an out-of-range page behaves per approved Q4.
- [ ] CRUD endpoints and behavior are unchanged; CRUD refreshes keep the
      current view, clamping the page into range when the result set shrank
      (approved Q7).
- [ ] `GET /books` without parameters still returns the exact unfiltered
      response.
- [ ] Maintained documentation describes the pagination contract and
      client paging behavior as landed.

## Supporting details

- This is the slice that makes larger collections practical: payloads stay
  bounded because the server never returns more than one page when pagination
  parameters are present.
- pytest seeding becomes cheap here: the isolation fixture from `010`
  (main decision D5) restores `server.app.BOOKS`, so tests can seed dozens of
  books without cleanup.
- The pager must derive its bounds from envelope metadata (`pageCount`),
  never from the row count of the current page alone.
- If this slice executes before `010`/`020`, it lands the discovery envelope
  itself and later slices adopt it — the envelope rule is defined by parameter
  presence, not slice order.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Approach: extend `server/query.py` with page slicing over the selected set and
total counting; parse `page` (and the size constant) in `server/app.py` and
emit `page`/`pageCount`/`total` per the approved envelope. In `Books.vue`, add
prev/next controls with a `Page X of Y` indicator, clamp/reset per approved
Q4, and keep CRUD refetches on the current (clamped) page.

Tasks:

- [ ] Implement page slicing + totals in `server/query.py`; `page` parsing and
      envelope metadata in `server/app.py` per approved Q1–Q4.
- [ ] Add the pager to `Books.vue` with bound-aware disabled states and the
      approved reset/clamp rules.
- [ ] Keep CRUD refetches on the current view with approved clamping.
- [ ] Tests: pytest (bounding, metadata, page over filtered/searched set,
      out-of-range behavior), component tests (pager bounds, page changes
      refetch, CRUD keeps clamped page), integration case for `page` over real
      HTTP.
- [ ] Rerun the unfiltered compatibility regression.
- [ ] Update `docs/development/book-discovery.md` with the pagination
      contract.

Risks: pager correctness depends on envelope metadata shape (blocked until
Q1/Q2 approved); reset/clamp semantics blocked until Q4/Q7 approved; seeded
multi-page fixtures must exercise at least three pages to prove bounding on
both ends.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Pager UI is prev/next plus an indicator (no page-number selector) — minimal
  and sufficient for "move through bounded pages"; a page-size selector stays
  out of scope per the main file.
- Page size lives as a server constant (Q3), not a client concern, so bounds
  have a single source of truth.
- No new open questions originate here beyond main-file Q1–Q7.

### Documentation

- Updates `docs/development/book-discovery.md`: pagination parameters, page
  size constant, envelope metadata, reset/clamp rules, and the unchanged
  unfiltered contract.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Server slicing, totals, and envelope metadata implemented per approved
      answers.
- [ ] Pager implemented with bounds, reset, and clamp rules.
- [ ] CRUD refetch paths keep the clamped current page.
- [ ] pytest, component, and integration tests added and passing.
- [ ] Unfiltered compatibility regression rerun and green.
- [ ] Spec page updated.

### Requirement verification

- Bounding at the API boundary → pytest: a seeded multi-page collection
  returns exactly the requested slice, correct `page`/`pageCount`/`total`, and
  composes with `read`/`q` when present; out-of-range and sub-1 pages behave
  per approved Q4.
- Unfiltered compatibility → pytest regression: parameter-less `GET /books`
  unchanged.
- Pager consistency at the UI boundary → component test: indicator matches the
  served page, prev/next disable at bounds, page changes refetch with `page`,
  filter/search changes reset per Q4, CRUD refetch keeps the clamped page.
- Transport agreement → integration case: `getBooks({ page })` (and combined
  parameter sets) against the live Flask process returns the expected bounded
  envelope.
- CRUD preservation → existing mutation tests pass unchanged; component test
  asserts refetches carry `page` with approved clamping.
- Documentation currency → spec statements match landed behavior in the same
  change.

# URL state sharing and view consistency

Make the full discovery state shareable and restorable through the `/books`
URL: serialize the combined filter/search/page state into query parameters,
restore it on load (including invalid and out-of-range values), keep browser
back/forward consistent, and prove the table, active controls, empty state,
and CRUD refreshes stay consistent across every state.

Parent Task: `tasks/20260920-books-page-discovery/000-main.md`

Depends On: `tasks/20260920-books-page-discovery/010-read-status-filter.md`, `tasks/20260920-books-page-discovery/020-title-author-search.md`, `tasks/20260920-books-page-discovery/030-bounded-pagination.md`

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] The full discovery state (read filter, search text, page) serializes
      into `/books` query parameters and restores from them on load; the
      default state produces no discovery parameters in the URL (main decision
      D2).
- [ ] Browser back/forward keeps the table, active controls, empty state, and
      pager consistent with the restored view (main decision D6 governs
      push/replace).
- [ ] Invalid or out-of-range URL state restores to the approved defined
      state (main-file Q4).
- [ ] Active controls reflect restored and navigated state — no drift between
      the URL and what the controls show.
- [ ] CRUD refreshes after restore keep the restored view (current query,
      clamped page per approved Q7).
- [ ] A shared URL's discovery state round-trips through the real client API
      and Flask server (integration).
- [ ] Documentation is finalized: the spec covers URL sharing/restoration, and
      the root README reflects the completed discovery capability.

## Supporting details

- This slice owns the cross-cutting consistency requirement: it is the single
  decisive check for "table, active controls, empty state, browser navigation,
  and CRUD refreshes stay consistent with the selected view" across the
  combined state.
- URL sync is built once here over the final combined state shape rather than
  as three partial serializations (main decision D1); the parameters and
  defaults it maps were defined by the earlier slices.
- Component tests must mount `Books.vue` with a real router using
  `createMemoryHistory()` (main decision D4) so restore and navigation run
  through real router behavior; memory history faithfully represents our sync
  logic — the router library owns the browser history internals.
- `Books.vue` is not router-aware today; this slice introduces the
  route-query ↔ discovery-state mapping and the push/replace discipline.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Approach: in `Books.vue`, map discovery state ↔ `route.query` in one place:
restore state from the route before the first fetch, `push` on discrete
control changes (filter, page) and debounced-`replace` for search typing
(main decision D6), and react to route changes (back/forward) by re-fetching
with the restored state. Omit default values from the URL. Handle
invalid/out-of-range restores per approved Q4 before fetching.

Tasks:

- [ ] Implement the route-query ↔ discovery-state mapping and restore-on-load
      in `Books.vue` (including invalid/out-of-range handling per approved Q4).
- [ ] Wire push/replace URL writing per main decision D6.
- [ ] React to route navigation (back/forward) by restoring state and
      refetching.
- [ ] Keep CRUD refetches consistent with the restored view (clamped page).
- [ ] Component tests with memory-history router: serialize/restore, back/
      forward, invalid-state restore, controls-in-sync, CRUD-after-restore,
      and the decisive combined scenario (fresh → filtered → searched → paged
      → shared-link restore → back/forward → mutate, asserting table,
      controls, empty state, and pager at each step).
- [ ] Integration case: the exact parameter sets the URL mapping produces
      round-trip through `getBooks` against the live Flask process.
- [ ] Finalize `docs/development/book-discovery.md` (URL state section) and
      refresh the root `README.md`.

Risks: router-sync bugs classically appear as feedback loops (state → URL →
state); the mapping must be idempotent and tested for loops. Restore-before-
fetch ordering matters for the first paint; the combined scenario asserts it.
Invalid-state behavior is blocked until Q4 is approved.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- One mapping function owns state ↔ query serialization in the component;
  `040` does not re-implement per-param logic from earlier slices.
- Restore resolves invalid/out-of-range values before fetching so the first
  request already carries the corrected state (per approved Q4).
- No new open questions originate here beyond main-file Q1–Q7.

### Documentation

- Finalizes `docs/development/book-discovery.md` with the URL state contract
  (parameters, defaults omitted, restore rules) and refreshes the root
  `README.md` so its Books page description covers the completed capability
  set — claims added only for behavior this change makes true.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Route-query mapping, restore, and navigation reactivity implemented.
- [ ] Push/replace writing and default-omission implemented.
- [ ] Invalid/out-of-range restore behavior implemented per approved Q4.
- [ ] Component tests including the decisive combined scenario added and
      passing.
- [ ] Integration round-trip case added and passing.
- [ ] Spec page finalized; README refreshed.

### Requirement verification

- URL serialize/restore → component tests with memory-history router through
  the real router: mounting on `/books?read=false&q=dune&page=2` restores
  controls, table, and pager; default state yields a clean URL.
- Browser navigation → component tests driving `router.push`/`router.back()`:
  each navigation restores a consistent view (decisive evidence for the
  navigation requirement; real browser E2E stays out of scope as recorded in
  the main file).
- Invalid/out-of-range restore → component tests asserting the approved Q4
  outcomes.
- Controls-in-sync → component tests asserting control values match the URL
  after restore and after navigation, in both directions.
- CRUD-after-restore → component test: mutate following a restored view and
  assert the refetch reuses the restored query with clamping per Q7.
- Shared-state round-trip → integration case: parameter sets produced by the
  URL mapping against the live Flask process return the expected envelopes —
  proves the mapping and the server agree over real HTTP.
- Combined view consistency → the decisive all-states scenario test listed in
  the tasks, crossing the real component + real router with the api module
  mocked at the transport boundary.
- Documentation currency → spec and README statements match landed behavior in
  the same change.

Task structure is created — only `tasks/` was added, nothing else touched. Here's the plan for approval.

## Structure created

`tasks/20260920-notes-query-capability/` — one main task plus three subtasks, decomposed along the three independently maintained compatibility boundaries (per `AGENTS.md` project context), not by files or test levels:

- **`000-main.md`** — requirements checklist (R1–R7), decision register, cross-boundary plan, requirement→evidence mapping
- **`010-service-query-api.md`** — the capability on `GET /notes/` + the contract specification; no dependencies (contract-first)
- **`020-client-query-support.md`** — `NotesClient.list_notes()` optional params; depends on 010
- **`030-cli-query-command.md`** — `notes list` flags; depends on 010 and 020

The dependency declarations make any other execution order unsafe — that's how "contract stable before consumers rely on it" is enforced structurally, and why the CLI's production-path test must run the real package from 020.

## Approach

Freeze one HTTP contract, implement it once per boundary in order 010 → 020 → 030, with evidence crossing each boundary's real public path. Key finding from inspection: client and CLI tests currently only cross fakes — nothing proves the production chain today, which is exactly what 030's decisive test closes (installed console script → `from_environment()` → real httpx → real running service, no injected client).

## Material decisions (recommended, need your approval)

1. Extend the existing `GET /notes/` route with optional params rather than a new endpoint
2. `limit`/`offset` with server-enforced `LIMIT_MAX` (100) rather than cursors
3. Out-of-range values → `422`, not silent clamping
4. **Bounded-vs-preserved resolution**: bounds apply only when `limit` is supplied; absent `limit` still returns every note — a default page size would silently truncate the collection for existing consumers
5. Deterministic ordering (`<field> <dir>, id ASC` tiebreaker) guaranteed for any parameterized query; the unparameterized request keeps today's exact behavior with no new ordering guarantee
6. `q` = case-insensitive substring over `title`/`description` (SQLite `LIKE` is ASCII-only — documented, not hidden)
7. One-to-one naming across all three boundaries (`limit/offset/sort/order/q` / `--limit --offset --sort --order --q`)
8. Bare JSON array response retained (no envelope → no total count; recorded consequence)
9. `notes-client` and `notes-cli` bump to `0.2.0` in the same change

No requirement questions are open — the request fixes the outcomes; the decisions above choose within them.

## Acceptance evidence

Service: integration tests over the public route (bounds rejection, tie-collision sort stability, filter semantics, unparameterized equivalence). Client: request-mapping component tests + one real-HTTP integration test. CLI: parser unit tests + the production-path run. Existing tests at all three boundaries stay green unchanged.

## Documentation

Spec at `docs/notes-query.md` (service owns the HTTP contract; `docs/development/index.md` currently records its absence) plus root/client/CLI READMEs, each landing in the same change as the behavior it describes.

## Risks

Shared `./notes.db` across service tests (mitigate with unique seeded data); ASCII-only case-folding must be documented, not silently promised; spec/implementation drift guarded by tests pinning the documented values.

## Exclusions

No schema changes, auth, cursors, envelopes, new subcommands/endpoints, or unreachable-service error behavior (unspecified today, not invented). Nothing implemented — plan is `Status: Draft`.

Execution waits for your approval. If you adjust any decision, I'll revise the affected subtask files and the plan returns to Draft.
