# Books discovery for larger collections

Plan and coordinate server-backed discovery for the Books page: read-status
filtering, title/author search, bounded pagination, URL persistence, and
consistent refresh behavior across the table, controls, empty state, browser
navigation, and existing CRUD operations.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] The Books page lets users filter by read status, search by title or
  author, and move through bounded pages of results.
- [ ] The complete discovery state is shareable and restorable through the
  `/books` URL, including direct loads and browser back/forward navigation.
- [ ] The table, active controls, empty state, page bounds, and CRUD refreshes
  all represent the same selected discovery view.
- [ ] Existing add, update, and delete behavior remains available, and each
  mutation refreshes the selected view rather than silently reverting to an
  unrelated list.
- [ ] `GET /books` without discovery parameters remains compatible with the
  existing response and returns the complete unfiltered collection; existing
  mutation routes remain compatible.

## Scope and workstreams

The work is split by independently owned contracts rather than by every
technical layer:

Both children include their focused tests and the documentation they own.
The parent retains the cross-boundary acceptance check and the final
requirement evidence.

Out of scope: sorting, bulk actions, changes to book persistence, new
mutation operations, authentication, and a redesign of the existing CRUD
forms or table beyond what discovery consistency requires.

## Subtasks

- [ ] `tasks/20260920-books-discovery/010-api-query-contract.md` — own
  server-side selection, pagination boundaries, response metadata, and
  unfiltered API compatibility.
- [ ] `tasks/20260920-books-discovery/020-books-page-discovery-state.md` —
  own client transport mapping, Vue state/rendering, router query
  synchronization, browser navigation, and CRUD refresh behavior.

## Unresolved requirement questions and decisions

These questions affect public API or user-visible URL contracts and must be
resolved before execution is approved:

1. What query parameter names and values are public for status, search, page,
   and page size? Recommendation: use stable, descriptive names shared by the
   API and URL, with an explicit all/read/unread status vocabulary.
2. What page size and pagination response shape should be public?
   Recommendation: keep `status` and `books` at the existing response
   boundary, add explicit pagination metadata, and use a documented default
   page size.
3. Should search be a case-insensitive substring match over either title or
   author, and how should blank/whitespace-only search be treated?
   Recommendation: normalize it as a case-insensitive substring search and
   treat blank input as no search.
4. When a mutation makes the current page empty or invalid, should the client
   clamp to the nearest valid page before refreshing or refresh the current
   page and then correct it? Recommendation: clamp using the server's
   pagination metadata so the URL and rendered view converge on a valid page.

Implementation decisions already made for planning:

- Selection and pagination belong on the server so the page does not fetch the
  entire collection as it grows.
- The URL is the shareable source of discovery state; the component must
  initialize from it and react to router history changes.
- There is no separate testing or documentation child: evidence and maintained
  guidance stay with the owner of the behavior they verify.

## Research and supporting facts

- `server/app.py` currently returns every item from `BOOKS` for `GET /books`
  and exposes unchanged `POST /books`, `PUT /books/<book_id>`, and
  `DELETE /books/<book_id>` routes.
- `server/query.py:list_books` currently only copies the input list, so there
  is no existing selection or pagination implementation to preserve.
- `client/src/api/books.js` already accepts an optional `params` object in
  `getBooks`, but the Books component does not pass one.
- `client/src/components/Books.vue` stores only a full `books` array, renders
  a table or `No books found.`, and refetches without any selected-view state
  after mutations.
- `client/src/router.js` has a `/books` route with history mode but no query
  state handling.
- `tests/test_books_api.py` covers only status codes for the unfiltered list
  and CRUD routes. `client/tests/Books.spec.js` covers only the empty state;
  `client/tests/books.integration.js` explicitly has no production transport
  integration coverage.
- `docs/development/index.md` currently says that no book-discovery
  specification exists, so the maintained developer guidance will need a
  focused update after the behavior is implemented.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

1. Resolve the public query vocabulary, default page size, metadata shape,
   search normalization, and invalid-page behavior.
2. Execute the API child to implement and test server-side filtering/search
   and bounded pagination while retaining the unfiltered response and CRUD
   routes.
3. Execute the client child against that contract to add URL-backed
   discovery state, controls, rendering, browser navigation handling, and
   mutation refreshes.
4. Run the parent cross-boundary checks: a real Flask HTTP request for the
   query contract, the mounted Books page with a real router for URL/history
   behavior, and the existing CRUD paths.
5. Update the maintained developer documentation with the settled API query
   contract and URL state behavior.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

The four questions above remain open. No implementation should begin until
the public contract is approved; changing it after the API and router work
starts would require reopening both children.

### Documentation

After implementation, update the smallest maintained page under
`docs/development/`—preferably the existing index if the contract remains
compact, otherwise one focused Books-discovery page linked from it. Document
the supported query parameters, response metadata, URL state, default
behavior, and the fact that an unparameterized `GET /books` remains
compatible. This planning change does not create or claim current product
guidance.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Resolve and record the public discovery contract.
- [ ] Approve this plan and both child plans.
- [ ] Complete `tasks/20260920-books-discovery/010-api-query-contract.md`.
- [ ] Complete `tasks/20260920-books-discovery/020-books-page-discovery-state.md`.
- [ ] Run the parent cross-boundary verification and existing CRUD regression
  checks.
- [ ] Publish the maintained developer documentation.
- [ ] Append immutable completion notes with evidence and any deferred scope.

### Requirement verification

- Requirements 1 and 5: server tests exercise the real Flask `GET /books`
  boundary for each filter/search combination, pagination boundaries, and the
  no-parameter response; existing mutation tests continue to pass.
- Requirements 1 and 3: mounted Books-page tests exercise active controls,
  table contents, filtered empty state, disabled/enabled page navigation, and
  the selected query passed through the production API module.
- Requirements 2 and 3: a router-backed client integration test starts at a
  query-bearing `/books` URL, verifies restored controls and results, changes
  discovery state, and verifies browser back/forward restoration.
- Requirement 4: component/integration coverage performs add, update, and
  delete through the existing production methods while a non-default
  discovery view is selected, then verifies that the refreshed results and
  URL remain coherent, including the last-item/page-bound case.

### Additional implementation verification

- Run the existing Python API suite and the client Vitest suite after focused
  coverage is added.
- Confirm no request path used by the existing unfiltered client call requires
  new parameters or a new response envelope.

# Synchronize Books discovery state with the URL

Build the client-owned discovery experience on top of the approved list API:
controls, selected-page rendering, URL sharing/restoration, browser history,
and CRUD refreshes that remain inside the selected view.

Parent Task: tasks/20260920-books-discovery/000-main.md

Depends On: tasks/20260920-books-discovery/010-api-query-contract.md

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] The Books page exposes the approved read-status filter, title/author
  search, and bounded page controls.
- [ ] Active controls, table rows, empty state, and page controls all derive
  from one approved discovery state.
- [ ] The approved discovery state is encoded in `/books` query parameters,
  restored on direct navigation, and restored by browser back/forward.
- [ ] Changing discovery controls updates the URL and fetches the matching
  server view without leaving stale results or stale active controls.
- [ ] Add, update, and delete continue to use the existing CRUD behavior and
  refresh the currently selected view, including when a mutation changes
  whether an item belongs on the current page.

## Scope and ownership

This child owns the client API parameter mapping, component state,
rendering/controls, router query synchronization, history behavior, and
client-side CRUD refresh orchestration. It owns the mounted component and
router evidence for these interactions. The server query implementation and
its HTTP contract belong to the API child.

## Unresolved requirement questions and decisions

- URL key names, value vocabulary, default omission/canonicalization, search
  normalization, page size, and out-of-range behavior are inherited from the
  parent and API child; do not create a second client-only vocabulary.
- Decide whether search updates are committed on every input or through an
  approved debounce. This is a UX detail that must not compromise direct-load
  or back/forward restoration.
- Decide whether a control change replaces or pushes history entries after the
  contract is settled. Recommendation: use the router behavior that makes
  deliberate discovery states restorable without creating unusable history
  noise, and verify it explicitly.

## Research and supporting facts

- `client/src/api/books.js:getBooks` already accepts an optional Axios
  `params` object, so the transport extension can remain compatible with
  existing unfiltered callers.
- `Books.vue` currently fetches once on mount and replaces its local full list
  after each mutation; it has no controls, pagination metadata, route
  watcher, or loading/error state.
- `router.js` uses `createWebHistory` and exposes `/books`, which provides the
  route boundary needed for query restoration and browser navigation tests.
- Current client tests mock every API function and only assert the empty
  state. The new tests must add router-backed behavior without making the
  existing CRUD methods test-only shortcuts.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

1. Consume the API child’s approved query and response metadata contract.
2. Establish one normalized discovery-state model with canonical defaults and
   conversion in both directions: route query to state and state to route
   query.
3. Extend `getBooks` usage to send the selected state and retain the returned
   page metadata.
4. Add status/search/page controls whose active values, disabled bounds,
   table, and empty state all derive from the current fetched view.
5. Watch or otherwise subscribe to route query changes so direct loads and
   browser back/forward restore the complete view without stale data.
6. Refactor add/update/delete refreshes to request the current discovery state,
   then handle an invalidated page according to the approved API behavior.
7. Add component and router-backed integration tests for controls, URL
   restoration, history, empty views, page bounds, and CRUD refreshes.
8. Update the maintained developer guidance with the URL-facing behavior.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

The client must not maintain a second interpretation of the API vocabulary.
Resolve the inherited contract first, then record the canonical URL and
history behavior here before execution.

### Documentation

Document the shareable `/books` query state, defaults, direct-load behavior,
browser navigation behavior, and how CRUD refreshes preserve the selected
view. Cross-link the API query contract rather than copying server details
that may diverge.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Resolve the inherited API contract and client history/debounce choices.
- [ ] Mark this child `Approved` after its dependency is complete or the
  approved contract is otherwise available.
- [ ] Add query/state conversion and production API parameter mapping.
- [ ] Implement controls, table state, empty state, and bounded pagination.
- [ ] Implement direct-load and browser history restoration.
- [ ] Preserve discovery state across add/update/delete refreshes.
- [ ] Add and run focused component/router integration tests.
- [ ] Update the maintained client guidance.
- [ ] Append completion notes with evidence and any deferred UX decisions.

### Requirement verification

- The decisive rendering check mounts the real `Books.vue` with a real
  router, supplies approved API responses, and asserts active controls,
  current-page rows, empty state, and disabled/enabled navigation.
- The decisive URL check starts from a query-bearing `/books` route, verifies
  restored state, changes state through controls, then exercises router
  back/forward and verifies both the URL and fetched/rendered view.
- The decisive CRUD check invokes the existing add/update/delete methods while
  a non-default discovery state is active, verifies requests retain that
  state, and covers a mutation that invalidates the current last page.

### Additional implementation verification

- Verify canonical defaults do not create URL churn or lose meaningful state
  during route synchronization.
- Verify rapid route changes cannot leave a result from an older discovery
  state displayed as the current view, if the chosen request orchestration
  permits overlapping requests.
- Verify the existing unfiltered mount and CRUD behavior continue to work for
  callers that do not provide discovery parameters.

- What stable ordering should pagination use? The current API exposes the
  in-memory insertion order; retaining that order is the least surprising
  compatibility choice unless a different order is required.
- Must the no-parameter `GET /books` response remain byte-for-byte in shape
  (the existing `status` and `books` keys only), or may compatible pagination
  metadata be added? The plan assumes the legacy no-parameter response stays
  unchanged and discovery requests carry any new metadata, pending approval.
- When a filter/search change leaves the current page invalid, should the page
  reset to one. When deleting the last result on a page, should the view move
  to the last remaining page. These choices affect the URL and CRUD refresh
  behavior.
- Should default discovery values be omitted from canonical URLs, and is page
  size user-selectable or an implementation constant?

## Research and supporting facts

- `server/app.py` currently serves all in-memory `BOOKS` from `GET /books`;
  it parses no query parameters and returns `{"status": "success", "books":
  BOOKS}`. The same module owns the existing POST, PUT, and DELETE routes.
- `server/query.py:list_books` currently returns a shallow list copy and is the
  natural server-side selection boundary.
- `client/src/api/books.js:getBooks` already accepts an optional `params`
  object, but `client/src/components/Books.vue` never supplies one.
- `Books.vue` currently stores only the returned books, renders a table or the
  fixed `No books found.` empty state, and refetches without parameters after
  each mutation.
- `client/src/router.js` already provides a history-mode `/books` route, so
  query state can be owned by the existing router instead of introducing a
  second navigation mechanism.
- Existing API coverage only checks a successful list and CRUD status codes.
  Existing client coverage checks the empty state; the integration file
  explicitly has no production transport coverage.
- `docs/development/index.md` currently states that no book-discovery
  specification exists. No current user-facing discovery documentation
  should be fabricated during this planning-only change.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Implement the feature across the two owned boundaries after the open contract
questions are answered:

1. Establish the approved query/response and URL contract, including matching,
   ordering, page bounds, invalid-state normalization, and compatibility
   behavior.
2. Complete the server workstream. Normalize optional discovery inputs, select
   by read status and title/author search, paginate within the approved bounds,
   and return the metadata the client needs. Keep the no-parameter list path
   and all mutation routes compatible. Add Flask-client tests at the actual
   HTTP boundary.
3. Complete the client workstream after the server contract is fixed. Derive
   one normalized discovery state from router query parameters, send that
   state through `getBooks`, and keep controls, table, empty state, page
   controls, and route updates synchronized. Make browser back/forward restore
   the same state without watcher loops or stale local state.
4. Refactor the existing CRUD refreshes to reload the current discovery
   request. Apply the approved page-normalization rule when a mutation removes
   or moves the last visible result, while preserving existing mutation calls
   and response handling.
5. Add focused client component/router coverage and a production-path
   transport check for query serialization. Run the existing API and client
   suites, then update the maintained developer documentation with the
   approved public API and URL contract.

The server workstream is a prerequisite for the client workstream because the
client state and tests depend on the agreed response metadata. Neither
workstream should add a client-side fetch-all/filter workaround: the purpose
of the API contract is to keep large collections bounded.

## Risks and boundaries

- Two sources of truth (local component state and `route.query`) could drift;
  the client task must define one-way synchronization and a canonicalization
  rule before adding controls.
- Filtering or mutating while a request is in flight can display a response
  for an older view. Tests should cover the chosen request-order strategy if
  the implementation introduces concurrent refreshes.
- Adding metadata to an unfiltered response could break strict existing
  consumers even if `books` remains present. Compatibility must be tested
  explicitly rather than inferred from the client.
- Pagination after CRUD can leave the current URL pointing at an empty or
  invalid page. The approved normalization rule must be applied consistently
  by API and UI.
- The task does not authorize changes to persistence, authentication,
  sorting beyond what is needed for stable paging, or unrelated router
  routes.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- The parent is split into two subtasks because the server discovery contract
  is an independently owned API result and the Vue page has an independently
  owned URL/rendering result. Verification and documentation stay with those
  owners.
- The plan remains Draft until the unresolved public API and URL semantics
  above are answered or explicitly delegated as implementation decisions.
- The planned implementation must preserve the existing no-query list path
  and CRUD endpoints; any response extension needs explicit compatibility
  evidence.

### Documentation

- No maintained documentation is changed in this planning-only pass.
- After implementation, update the smallest owned developer documentation
  location with the approved query parameters, response metadata, URL
  serialization, and navigation/mutation behavior. If a discovery spec is
  introduced, link it from `docs/development/index.md`; do not publish the
  target behavior as current guidance before it exists.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Resolve the open API, URL, matching, ordering, and page-transition
      questions.
- [ ] Approve this plan and change both child plans from Draft to Approved.
- [ ] Complete `tasks/20260920-books-discovery/010-server-discovery-query.md`.
- [ ] Complete `tasks/20260920-books-discovery/020-books-page-discovery.md`.
- [ ] Run the decisive API, client, and transport/navigation verification.
- [ ] Update maintained documentation and record completion evidence.

### Requirement verification

- **Read-status filtering and title/author search:** API integration tests
  should seed books covering each status and match location, exercise the
  production `GET /books` route with the approved parameters, and assert the
  page result and count metadata. A Books-page test should assert the same
  parameters are sent when controls change and that the table/active controls
  show only that view.
- **Bounded pagination:** API tests should assert page size, total/page
  metadata, stable ordering, and the approved invalid/out-of-range behavior.
  A rendered-page test should assert disabled/hidden boundary controls and
  that navigating a page updates both the request and table.
- **Share/restore and browser navigation:** mount the Books component with the
  real router configuration, load a URL containing the approved query state,
  and assert controls and results restore from it. Push at least two states,
  invoke router back/forward, and assert the complete view returns each time.
- **Consistent table, controls, empty state, and CRUD refresh:** exercise a
  non-default filtered/search page through the component's production API
  functions, then perform add/update/delete and assert refreshes retain the
  selected query and apply the approved page-transition rule. Include a
  no-match view whose empty state identifies the selected view without
  showing stale rows.
- **Unfiltered API and CRUD compatibility:** Flask test-client coverage must
  assert the no-parameter list response keeps the existing status/books
  contract and that POST, PUT, and DELETE retain their current status and
  response behavior. This check must not be satisfied by mocking the route.

# Server discovery query and compatibility contract

Define and implement the Flask-side selection, search, and bounded-pagination
contract for Books while retaining the legacy unfiltered list and CRUD
behavior. This is a planned subtask; implementation is **Not implemented**.

Parent Task: tasks/20260920-books-discovery/000-main.md

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] `GET /books` accepts the approved optional read-status and
      title/author-search inputs and composes them against the same collection.
- [ ] Discovery requests return bounded pages with stable ordering and the
      approved metadata and invalid-input behavior.
- [ ] A no-parameter `GET /books` remains compatible with the existing
      unfiltered response contract.
- [ ] Existing POST, PUT, and DELETE routes keep their current behavior and
      response compatibility.
- [ ] Flask test-client coverage proves the discovery and compatibility
      boundaries without bypassing the HTTP route.

## Unresolved requirement questions

This subtask inherits the parent questions that affect the public API. Before
execution, confirm the parameter names/values, search matching rules, default
and maximum page sizes, ordering, invalid-page behavior, metadata shape, and
whether legacy no-parameter responses may gain keys. The server contract must
not silently choose a public behavior that the parent has left open.

## Research and supporting facts

- `server/app.py` owns the `/books` GET/POST route and the `/books/<book_id>`
  PUT/DELETE route.
- `server/query.py:list_books(books)` is currently an identity-style list
  helper and has no query or pagination model.
- The current list response contains `status: "success"` and the complete
  `books` array. Existing API tests do not assert the response body, so
  compatibility assertions need to be added.
- The collection is an in-memory module-level list. The implementation should
  preserve its current mutation semantics unless the approved behavior
  requires a narrowly scoped test-isolation adjustment.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

1. Record the approved query names, normalized values, default/max bounds,
   stable ordering, page metadata, and no-parameter compatibility rule.
2. Extend the query boundary so filtering and search happen before pagination,
   with the same normalized selection logic used by the route.
3. Update the GET route to distinguish the legacy no-parameter path from
   discovery requests as required by the compatibility decision. Keep
   mutation methods and their response shapes unchanged.
4. Add test data with read/unread books and title/author matches, then cover
   status-only, search-only, combined, empty, first/last, and invalid-page
   requests through Flask's test client.
5. Add a regression assertion for the existing no-parameter response and
   retain the existing CRUD checks.

The output of this subtask is the API contract and evidence that the client
can rely on it. It does not own router state or Vue rendering.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- The server should perform selection and pagination so large collections are
  not transferred to the browser merely to be filtered there.
- The exact public parameter and metadata names remain open until the parent
  plan is approved.
- No new persistence or sorting policy is authorized by this subtask; stable
  ordering must follow the approved compatibility choice.

### Documentation

- During implementation, document the approved GET query parameters,
  response metadata, bounds, and no-parameter compatibility rule in the
  smallest maintained developer-facing location owned by the server/API.
- Do not create a placeholder API page during this planning-only pass.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Resolve and record the approved server contract in the parent task.
- [ ] Mark this subtask Approved before implementation.
- [ ] Implement the query normalization, selection, and pagination boundary.
- [ ] Preserve and test the legacy list and CRUD routes.
- [ ] Record API test evidence and link any maintained documentation update.

### Requirement verification

- **Status/search selection:** Flask test-client requests against `GET
  /books` must prove each approved filter independently and in combination,
  including no-match results.
- **Bounded pages:** requests for the first, middle, last, and invalid pages
  must prove the approved page size, total/page metadata, stable ordering, and
  boundary behavior.
- **Unfiltered compatibility:** a no-query request must prove the legacy
  `status`/`books` contract and unfiltered contents; existing CRUD requests
  must still return their current success responses.

# Books page URL-backed discovery state

Connect the Vue Books page to the server discovery contract and make the
controls, table, empty state, pagination, browser navigation, and CRUD
refreshes share one URL-backed view state. This is a planned subtask;
implementation is **Not implemented**.

Parent Task: tasks/20260920-books-discovery/000-main.md

Depends On: tasks/20260920-books-discovery/010-server-discovery-query.md

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] The page exposes read-status and title/author search controls whose
      active values are visible and whose combination is sent to the API.
- [ ] The page renders bounded pagination from server metadata and keeps page
      controls within the approved range.
- [ ] The `/books` query string is the shareable/restorable source for the
      complete discovery state, and browser back/forward restores controls,
      results, pagination, and empty state.
- [ ] The table and empty state always represent the active discovery view;
      stale rows and stale active-control values are not retained.
- [ ] Add, update, and delete refresh the current discovery request, preserve
      the selected view, and apply the approved page-transition behavior.
- [ ] Existing client CRUD calls remain compatible with the existing API
      functions.
- [ ] Component, router, and client transport coverage proves the behavior
      through the production Books page path.

## Unresolved requirement questions

This subtask inherits the parent decisions about URL parameter names,
canonical omission of defaults, page reset/clamping, search semantics, and
post-CRUD page transitions. It must also confirm whether controls update the
URL on each input/change or on an explicit submit; the URL must remain the
single shareable state either way.

## Research and supporting facts

- `client/src/components/Books.vue` currently owns only `books` and calls
  `getBooks()` on mount and after each mutation. It has no controls, loading
  state, pagination metadata, or route access.
- `client/src/api/books.js:getBooks(params = {})` already passes an Axios
  `params` object to `/books`, so transport changes can remain localized.
- `client/src/router.js` uses Vue Router history mode with a `/books` route.
  Query parameters are available without adding a new route.
- Current client coverage only mounts the component with mocked API methods
  and checks `No books found.`; `client/tests/books.integration.js` has no
  production transport coverage.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

1. Record the approved URL serialization and canonicalization rules, then
   define one normalized discovery-state model containing filter, search,
   page, page size (if exposed), result metadata, and current rows.
2. Initialize that model from `route.query`, serialize control/page changes
   through the existing router, and watch route changes so direct links and
   browser back/forward reload the same view. Prevent route/component
   synchronization loops and discard or supersede stale responses according
   to the chosen request strategy.
3. Update `getBooks` calls to send the normalized server parameters. Render
   the active filter/search values, current table, no-match empty state, and
   bounded page controls from one response/state model.
4. Update add, edit, and remove flows to refetch with the current discovery
   parameters. Apply the approved reset/clamp rule when the mutation changes
   the number of matching pages, and update the URL whenever that rule changes
   the page.
5. Add focused component tests for controls and empty/table states, router
   tests for direct restoration and back/forward, and a transport test that
   verifies query serialization. Exercise CRUD refresh on a non-default view
   so the test does not pass by accidentally falling back to an unfiltered
   request.

The output of this subtask is the user-visible discovery experience. It
depends on the server subtask's final parameter and metadata contract and
does not change unrelated routes or API mutation semantics.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Router query state should be the canonical shareable state; local state may
  cache response data but must not become a second independent filter model.
- The page must retain the selected filter/search while refreshing after CRUD;
  the exact handling of an emptied page remains a parent-level decision.
- The existing `getBooks(params)` seam is sufficient unless the approved
  response requires a narrowly scoped client transport adjustment.

### Documentation

- During implementation, document the user-facing URL parameters and the
  behavior of active controls, empty results, browser navigation, and
  mutation refreshes in the smallest maintained Books/developer guide.
- Do not publish this target behavior as current documentation during the
  planning-only pass.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Resolve and record the approved URL and page-transition contract in the
      parent task.
- [ ] Wait for the approved server subtask contract.
- [ ] Mark this subtask Approved before implementation.
- [ ] Implement URL-backed state, controls, pagination, rendering, and CRUD
      refreshes.
- [ ] Add and run component, router/navigation, and transport evidence.
- [ ] Record documentation and verification results.

### Requirement verification

- **Controls and selected view:** mount the real Books component with an API
  response containing metadata, change status/search controls, and assert the
  generated request, active values, and table rows all describe the same
  view.
- **Pagination:** navigate within the rendered bounds and assert the route,
  request parameters, rows, and boundary control states change together.
- **URL restore/navigation:** start at a deep-link query, assert it restores
  the controls and result, then create multiple route states and verify
  browser back/forward restores each complete state.
- **Empty and CRUD refresh:** assert a no-match response renders the selected
  filter/search context without stale rows; perform CRUD on a filtered page
  and assert every refresh uses the current query and follows the approved
  page-transition rule.

producer_records.prompt: Migrate post author metadata from the current single-name field to a structured multi-author form without breaking existing content or generated pages during the transition. Templates, archives, feeds, and authoring tools must move to the new model, existing posts must be migrated safely, and the legacy form may be rejected only after generated-output and content evidence show that nothing still depends on it. Plan the work and create the appropriate task structure without implementing it.
producer_records.response:
Task structure created under `tasks/20260920-post-author-migration/` — a main task plus three subtasks, one per compatibility state. Nothing was implemented; all plans are `Status: Draft` and execution waits.

## What I found

- Legacy model: `author: "<name>"` string front matter in both posts (`first.md`, `second.md`).
- Consumers: `_includes/layouts/post.njk:2` (page) and `content/feed.xml.njk:5` (feed). `scripts/new-post.js:1` emits the legacy form.
- Archives/tag pages/home/sitemap render no author data (`postslist.njk` is title+URL only) — verified non-consumers.
- Both test files are comment-only stubs; no executable generated-output coverage exists, and `node_modules/` isn't installed.

## Structure and approach

- **`000-main.md`** — requirements, two open requirement questions, verified current-state facts, orchestration plan.
- **`010-multi-author-model-and-compat.md`** (dual-read state): introduce `authors` + legacy normalization via computed data, move layout and feed templates to the new model, replace the test stubs with real production-build tests (temp output dir; multi-author fixtures built from temp content copies, never the real `content/`). Existing legacy content must render byte-identically.
- **`020-content-and-tooling-migration.md`**: migrate both posts and the authoring tool; equivalence evidence via the exact-string tests; record the content audit as gate input; document the new form in the same change.
- **`030-evidence-gate-and-legacy-rejection.md`**: three-part recorded gate (zero legacy keys, green suite, tool emits new form only) must be green *before* enabling build-time rejection, removing the legacy fallback, and adding an integration test proving a legacy fixture fails the real build.

The user-stated gate is encoded structurally: 030 depends on 010 + 020 and its first checklist item blocks rejection until evidence is recorded.

## Decisions and open questions needing your input

1. **Q1 — field shape (material, persisted format):** `authors: ["Ada Example"]` list of names (recommended) vs. list of objects like `{ name, url }`.
2. **Q2 — archive scope:** keep archive/tag pages as verified non-consumers with unchanged output (recommended), or start displaying authors there (new visible behavior, extends 010).

Also pending your approval: field name `authors`; build-time rejection in `eleventy.config.js`; multi-author page display joined with `", "`; README "Adding posts" section as the documentation home.

## Acceptance evidence (planned)

Generated-output tests through the real Eleventy build assert exact author strings across all three states (before/after equivalence), temp-copy multi-author fixtures prove new-form rendering on page and feed, and the rejection is proven by a real build failing on a legacy fixture while real content passes.

## Risks / exclusions

Computed-data visibility on `post.data` inside the feed is a verified-with-real-build risk with a filter fallback; `npm install` must succeed or build evidence is reported as not run; test fixtures stay out of tracked content. Excluded: no new archive author display (pending Q2), no `docs/index.md` or placeholder docs, `docs/development/index.md` left untouched.

Answer Q1/Q2 (or approve the recommendations) and I'll update the requirements and mark the plans `Approved` — execution starts only after that.

# Migrate post author metadata to structured multi-author form Migrate post author metadata from the legacy single-name `author` front-matter string to a structured multi-author form across templates, archives, feeds, and the authoring tool, migrating existing posts safely and rejecting the legacy form only after generated-output and content evidence shows nothing still depends on it. Scope note: this task plans and tracks the migration. These files do not authorize execution; every plan below is `Draft` and execution waits on explicit approval plus resolution of the requirement questions. ## Requirements checklist - [ ] Posts support a structured multi-author field as the supported content model; a post can declare multiple named authors. (Field shape pending requirement question Q1.) - [ ] Every consumer of post author metadata — post page template, feed, archive/tag surfaces, and the authoring tool — reads only the new model in the final state. (Archive display scope pending requirement question Q2.) - [ ] At every executed state of the migration, the production build succeeds and generated output for existing content (post pages, blog archive, tag pages, feed, sitemap) remains correct; existing posts end up migrated to the new form. - [ ] The legacy single-name `author` form is rejected by the production build only after generated-output and content evidence shows that no source content, template, tooling, or generated output still depends on it. - [ ] Maintained documentation describes the new author form and, in the same reviewed change that enables it, the rejection of the legacy form. ## Requirement questions - **Q1 — Field shape (material; persisted content format).** Options: - **A (recommended):** `authors` is a list of author name strings, e.g. `authors: ["Ada Example", "Grace Example"]`. Smallest change that satisfies "structured multi-author"; rendering semantics stay name-text-only. - **B:** `authors` is a list of objects, e.g. `authors: [{ name: "...", url: "..." }]`. Leaves room for per-author metadata (links, ids) but introduces fields no current template renders. - **Q2 — Archive display scope.** The blog archive and tag pages currently render only title and URL (`_includes/postslist.njk`) and consume no author data. Does "archives must move to the new model" mean: - **A (recommended):** archives are verified as non-consumers and their output stays unchanged; no new author display is added. - **B:** archive/tag pages must start displaying author names from the new model (new visible behavior, extends subtask 010 scope). ## Subtasks - [ ] tasks/20260920-post-author-migration/010-multi-author-model-and-compat.md - [ ] tasks/20260920-post-author-migration/020-content-and-tooling-migration.md - [ ] tasks/20260920-post-author-migration/030-evidence-gate-and-legacy-rejection.md ## Supporting facts Current state, verified by inspection (2026-09-20): - Legacy form: `author: ""` string in post front matter. `content/posts/first.md` (`Ada Example`), `content/posts/second.md` (`Grace Example`). These are the only content files. - Consumers of author data: - `_includes/layouts/post.njk:2` — `

{{ author }}

`. - `content/feed.xml.njk:5` — simplified Atom-like document; renders `{{ post.data.author }}` inside ``; `layout: false`, permalink `/feed/feed.xml`. - Author non-consumers (verified): `_includes/postslist.njk` renders only title + URL and is shared by `content/blog.njk` (archive), `content/index.njk` (home), and `content/tag-pages.njk` (tag pages); `content/sitemap.xml.njk` renders URLs only; `content/posts/posts.json` sets layout/tags only. - Authoring tool: `scripts/new-post.js` exports `frontMatter(title, author)` emitting the legacy string form. No npm script invokes it. - Tests: `tests/author-output.test.js` and `tests/archive-output.test.js` are comment-only stubs; `npm test` (`node --test tests/*.test.js`) currently passes with no executable coverage. No generated-output coverage exists yet. - Dependencies are not installed (`node_modules/` absent, gitignored); build/test evidence requires `npm install` (devDependency `@11ty/eleventy ^3.0.0`). `_site/` is gitignored output. - Build config: `eleventy.config.js` — input `content/`, includes `../_includes`, output `_site`. - `docs/development/index.md` notes a missing archive pagination specification — unrelated to authors; leave unchanged. There is no `docs/index.md` and no existing documentation describes author metadata. - Fixture provenance: `UPSTREAM.md` (adapted from Eleventy Base Blog). ## Execution plan Status: Draft Three subtasks in strict order, one per compatibility state. Each ends with the site building green and its evidence recorded, so every executed state is independently acceptable. 1. **010 — dual-read state.** Introduce the structured `authors` model with a normalization path that maps legacy `author` strings into it, move the post layout and feed templates to read only the new model, and replace the two comment-only test stubs with real generated-output tests run through the production Eleventy build. Existing content stays legacy-form and its generated output must be byte-identical to the pre-change baseline. 2. **020 — migrated-content state.** Rewrite both posts' front matter to the new form and update `scripts/new-post.js` to emit it (multiple authors supported). Generated output for the two posts must remain identical; content audit shows zero legacy keys. Document the `authors` front-matter form for content authors in the same change. 3. **030 — rejection state.** Gate: content audit (zero legacy keys) plus full green generated-output suite plus tooling emitting only the new form. Only when all three hold, enable build-time rejection of legacy `author`, remove the legacy normalization fallback, add an integration test proving a legacy fixture fails the real build, and document the rejection in the same change. Sequencing rationale: the rejection gate required by the request is encoded as subtask 030's dependency on 010 + 020 and its explicit pre-rejection evidence checklist. Tests from 010 assert exact author strings at the generated-output boundary, so they stay valid across the internal migration and provide the before/after equivalence evidence for the "nothing breaks" constraint. Prerequisites and risks: - `npm install` must succeed before any build evidence; if it is blocked, report that build evidence is not run rather than claiming it. - Computed-data normalization must be visible on `post.data` inside the feed template; verified by the real-build feed test in 010, with a shared filter as the fallback mechanism. - Test fixture posts (multi-author cases) must be built in temp copies of the content tree, never added to the real `content/`, so the public site output is not altered by tests. - Q1 and Q2 must be resolved before 010 executes; both change requirements, not just implementation. ### Implementation decisions and open questions - **Open requirement questions:** Q1 (field shape) and Q2 (archive display scope) above. Neither is resolved by this plan; subtasks 010 and 020 depend on Q1, 010 depends on Q2. Recommendation: Q1=A, Q2=A. - **Decision (pending approval with the plan):** new field is named `authors`; legacy key is `author`. - **Decision:** rejection is enforced at build time by validating post front matter in `eleventy.config.js` (exact Eleventy 3 hook chosen during 030); the authoring tool additionally never emits the legacy form (from 020). - **Decision:** during the dual-read state, normalization maps legacy `author` to the new model via Eleventy computed data in `content/posts/posts.json`; a shared filter is the fallback if computed data is not visible on collection items in the feed. - **Decision:** multi-author display on post pages joins names with `", "`; the feed emits one `` element per author in post order. Affects only posts that opt into multiple authors; existing single-author output is unchanged. ### Documentation - Follows `docs/development/documentation.md` (read before restructuring). - No maintained documentation currently describes author metadata, so subtask 010 needs no documentation change (unless Q2 resolves to archive display). - Subtask 020 adds a short "Adding posts" section to `README.md` documenting the `authors` front-matter form — placed with the site entry point that content authors use; smallest structure that helps the reader (alternative considered: a new `docs/` page, rejected as unnecessary structure). - Subtask 030 updates the same README section, in the same reviewed change that enables rejection, so the "legacy form is rejected" claim is true when published. No placeholder pages or `docs/index.md` are created. ### Task checklist - [ ] Resolve Q1 and Q2 with the requester; update affected requirements. - [ ] Execute and complete tasks/20260920-post-author-migration/010-multi-author-model-and-compat.md - [ ] Execute and complete tasks/20260920-post-author-migration/020-content-and-tooling-migration.md - [ ] Verify 030's pre-rejection evidence gate is fully green before any rejection change lands. - [ ] Execute and complete tasks/20260920-post-author-migration/030-evidence-gate-and-legacy-rejection.md - [ ] Final review: full `npm test` + production build green; all requirement checkboxes in main and subtasks supported by recorded evidence. ### Requirement verification - Multi-author model supported → decisive evidence: production-build test with a multi-author fixture post (temp content copy) asserting all authors render on the post page and in the feed (subtask 010). - Consumers moved to the new model → decisive evidence: source audit shows no template or tool reads the legacy key, and the full generated-output suite passes after the legacy fallback is removed (subtasks 020 + 030). - No breakage during transition → decisive evidence: generated-output tests asserting exact author strings and archive contents pass against unchanged content before the model change, and pass again after each migration step (subtasks 010 and 020). - Legacy rejected only after evidence → decisive evidence: 030's recorded pre-rejection checklist (content audit zero legacy keys; green suite; tool emits new form only) followed by an integration test in which a legacy-form fixture fails the real build while the real content builds cleanly (subtask 030). The gate order itself is a requirement; it is enforced by subtask dependency plus the recorded checklist. - Documentation current with behavior → evidence: README section present in the same changes that introduce the new form (020) and enable rejection (030); verified by inspection of the merged state. ### Additional implementation verification - Verify computed-data visibility on `post.data` in the feed context via the real build early in 010 (material risk to the normalization approach). - Confirm the shared test build helper is exercised by every generated-output test (maintained test infrastructure verified through real consumers). - Confirm `node --test` collects all test files and exits cleanly after each subtask; record suite results in the executing subtask.

# Migrate existing posts and authoring tool to the new author model

Second migration state: move all source content and the authoring tool to the
structured `authors` form while legacy is still accepted, with generated
output for the existing posts unchanged, and document the new authoring form
for content authors.

Parent Task: tasks/20260920-post-author-migration/000-main.md
Depends On: tasks/20260920-post-author-migration/010-multi-author-model-and-compat.md

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] All source posts declare authors with the new `authors` form (shape per
      parent Q1); no post front matter carries the legacy `author` key.
- [ ] `scripts/new-post.js` emits the new form and supports multiple authors;
      its behavior is unit-tested.
- [ ] Generated output for the two migrated posts is unchanged after
      migration (equivalence evidence at the production-build boundary).
- [ ] Maintained documentation describes the `authors` front-matter form for
      content authors, updated in the same reviewed change that migrates the
      content.

## Supporting facts

- Only two posts exist: `content/posts/first.md` (`Ada Example`),
  `content/posts/second.md` (`Grace Example`).
- `scripts/new-post.js` exports `frontMatter(title, author)` returning
  legacy-form front matter; nothing invokes it from `package.json` scripts.
- After subtask 010, the generated-output suite (author + archive tests plus
  temp-fixture coverage) exists and is green; legacy content still builds via
  normalization.
- The content audit performed here (zero legacy `author` keys in `content/`)
  is a required input to subtask 030's rejection gate — record it, do not
  just observe it.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Approach:

1. Migrate `content/posts/first.md` and `content/posts/second.md` to the new
   `authors` form (each becomes a one-element list per Q1 shape). No other
   front-matter changes.
2. Update `scripts/new-post.js`: `frontMatter(title, authors)` accepts an
   ordered list of author names and emits the new form with correct YAML
   quoting; keep it dependency-free. Unit test: single author, multiple
   authors, and emitted front matter matches the form documented for content
   authors.
3. Equivalence evidence: run the full generated-output suite — the exact
   author strings asserted by the 010 baseline tests must pass unchanged
   after the content migration, proving no output regression.
4. Documentation (same change): add a short "Adding posts" section to
   `README.md` documenting the `authors` front-matter field with an example.
   At this state legacy `author` is still accepted, so the section describes
   the new form as the supported way to author posts without claiming legacy
   is rejected.
5. Content audit: confirm `content/` contains no legacy `author` keys
   (search for the singular key) and record the result — this is gate
   evidence for 030.
6. Verify: full `npm test` green; production build green; record results.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Open (parent): Q1 field shape determines the emitted front matter in both
  content and the tool.
- Local: tool signature takes an ordered author-name list; documentation home
  is a README section per the parent's documentation decision.

### Documentation

- README gains the "Adding posts" section in the same change as the content
  migration, per `docs/development/documentation.md` (claims describe current
  behavior; legacy is still accepted at this state, so the section must not
  claim it is rejected).

### Task checklist

- [ ] Migrate both posts' front matter to the new form.
- [ ] Update `scripts/new-post.js` for the new form (multi-author); add unit
      tests.
- [ ] Run generated-output suite; confirm exact-string equivalence.
- [ ] Add README "Adding posts" section documenting `authors`.
- [ ] Run content audit; record zero legacy keys as gate evidence for 030.
- [ ] Full suite + production build green; update requirement checkboxes.

### Requirement verification

- Content migrated → decisive: content audit shows zero legacy `author` keys
  in `content/posts/` (recorded).
- Tool emits new form → decisive: unit tests covering single and multiple
  authors against the documented form.
- Output equivalence → decisive: exact-string generated-output tests pass
  unchanged post-migration.
- Documentation current → decisive: README section present in the same change
  (inspection of the merged state).

### Additional implementation verification

- Confirm the audit search covers all of `content/`, not just `posts/`, so
  the 030 gate evidence is complete.

# Evidence gate, legacy rejection, and compatibility cleanup

Final migration state: verify nothing still depends on the legacy single-name
`author` form, then reject it at build time, remove the legacy read path, and
document the rejection — in that order, with the gate evidence recorded
before any rejection change lands.

Parent Task: tasks/20260920-post-author-migration/000-main.md
Depends On: tasks/20260920-post-author-migration/010-multi-author-model-and-compat.md
Depends On: tasks/20260920-post-author-migration/020-content-and-tooling-migration.md

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] Pre-rejection evidence is recorded and fully green before any rejection
      change: (a) content audit shows zero legacy `author` keys in `content/`
      (from 020), (b) the full generated-output suite passes rendering from
      the new model, (c) the authoring tool emits only the new form.
- [ ] Only after that evidence: the production build fails when a post's
      front matter carries the legacy `author` key, with a clear error
      message.
- [ ] The legacy normalization/fallback read path is removed in the same
      change as rejection; templates and the posts data file read only the
      new model.
- [ ] After rejection lands, the full generated-output suite and archive
      tests still pass, and an integration test proves a legacy-form fixture
      fails the real build while the real content builds cleanly.
- [ ] Documentation states the legacy form is rejected, updated in the same
      reviewed change that enables rejection.

## Supporting facts

- The rejection gate ("legacy may be rejected only after generated-output and
  content evidence") is a requirement from the original request, not a
  preference. Gate inputs: 020's recorded content audit, the 010-generated
  generated-output suite, and the 020 tooling tests.
- After 020, legacy support exists only as the normalization fallback added
  in 010 (`content/posts/posts.json` computed data or the shared filter) plus
  its acceptance in front matter.
- Rejection and fallback removal must land together: rejecting the form while
  keeping the fallback would leave dead code that still reads `author`.
- `npm test` runs `node --test tests/*.test.js`; the build helper from 010
  supports building an alternate input directory into a temp output — reused
  for the legacy-failure integration test.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Approach:

1. Gate check (blocking, recorded in this file before proceeding):
   - Content audit: search all of `content/` for legacy `author` keys —
     expect zero. (Reuse/verify the 020 audit; re-run it here rather than
     trusting a stale record.)
   - Run the full generated-output suite — expect green, rendering from the
     new model.
   - Confirm the authoring tool emits only the new form (020 unit tests).
   If any check fails, stop and report; do not enable rejection.
2. Implement build-time rejection: validate post front matter in
   `eleventy.config.js` (choose the Eleventy 3 hook during execution —
   e.g., a data preprocessor or collection/data check) so that any post
   carrying the legacy `author` key fails the build with a clear message.
   Export the validation predicate so it is unit-testable without bypassing
   the wired behavior.
3. Integration test at the real boundary: using the build helper, build a
   temp copy of the real site plus one legacy-form fixture post and assert
   the build fails with the rejection error; assert the real content (no
   legacy keys) still builds cleanly.
4. Remove the legacy normalization fallback (010's legacy branch), leaving
   the new model as the only read path. Re-run the full suite — the
   exact-string baseline tests must still pass, proving generated output is
   carried by the new model alone.
5. Documentation (same change): update the README "Adding posts" section to
   state that the legacy `author` form is no longer accepted and the build
   fails on it — true in the same reviewed change.
6. Final verification: full `npm test` green; `npm run build` green; record
   all results and complete the parent requirement checkboxes.

Boundaries: rejection and failure-path evidence come from the real Eleventy
build (temp-copy fixture), not from invoking the validator in isolation.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Local: exact Eleventy 3 hook for build-time validation (chosen during
  execution; exported predicate keeps it unit-testable); rejection triggers
  on presence of the legacy `author` key in post front matter regardless of
  value.
- No open requirement questions remain from the parent at this stage (Q1/Q2
  resolved before 010 executed).

### Documentation

- README "Adding posts" section is updated in the same reviewed change that
  enables rejection, per `docs/development/documentation.md` (claim becomes
  true in the same change that publishes it).

### Task checklist

- [ ] Run and record the three-part gate check (audit, suite, tooling) before
      any rejection change.
- [ ] Implement build-time rejection in `eleventy.config.js` with exported,
      unit-testable validation predicate.
- [ ] Add legacy-failure integration test (temp copy + fixture post; real
      build must fail; real content must pass).
- [ ] Remove legacy normalization fallback; re-run full suite.
- [ ] Update README to state legacy rejection (same change).
- [ ] Full suite + production build green; update requirement checkboxes in
      this file and the parent.

### Requirement verification

- Gate evidence before rejection → decisive: the recorded gate checklist in
  this file, completed and green before step 2 begins.
- Build rejects legacy form → decisive: integration test where a legacy
  fixture fails the real build and real content passes.
- Legacy read path removed → decisive: full generated-output suite green
  after removal, plus source audit showing no template/data-file reads of the
  legacy key.
- Documentation current → decisive: README rejection statement present in the
  same change enabling rejection (inspection of the merged state).

### Additional implementation verification

- Confirm the rejection error names the offending file/content so a content
  author can fix it without reading build internals.
- Confirm the rejection check cannot be skipped by the front-matter parser
  treating `author` as data in an unexpected shape (e.g., list value) —
  presence of the key is what triggers rejection.
