# Migrate post author metadata to structured multi-author data

Plan the transition from the single `author` front-matter string to an
ordered, structured multi-author model across source content, Eleventy
templates, generated artifacts, and the post-authoring helper while preserving
existing content and public pages during the compatibility window.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] Posts have a canonical structured representation that can express the
      ordered authors for a post, including the current single-author cases.
- [ ] Existing posts are migrated safely without losing titles, body content,
      routes, tags, layout behavior, or author display data.
- [ ] Post templates, home/blog/tag archive paths, and the feed consume the
      canonical author model; generated pages and feed output remain valid and
      preserve existing single-author behavior while representing multiple
      authors according to the approved public contract.
- [ ] The post-authoring helper emits the canonical metadata and no longer
      requires callers to author the legacy single-name field.
- [ ] The legacy field remains supported for the transition until source
      content and generated-output evidence demonstrate that no dependency
      remains; any rejection/removal is a separately verified final step.
- [ ] Tests exercise the real Eleventy production build and the authoring
      helper at the boundaries where the migration can regress.
- [ ] Maintained user/developer guidance describes the supported authoring
      format and transition state after implementation.

## Scope and workstreams

The migration is organized into four dependent workstreams:

1. Establish the canonical data shape, a transition normalizer/compatibility
   policy, and migrate the checked-in posts.
2. Move the post layout, shared archive rendering, and feed generation to the
   canonical model while preserving public routes and valid output.
3. Update the authoring helper and its contract so newly created posts use the
   new model.
4. Run the integrated source/output audit and authorize legacy rejection only
   when the evidence gate passes.

The work includes the existing Eleventy source tree, checked-in post content,
the `scripts/new-post.js` helper, generated-output tests, and maintained
guidance. It excludes unrelated archive pagination and unrelated upstream
fixture changes.

## Requirement questions and decisions

- The request does not specify the exact structured schema. The recommended
  direction is an ordered `authors` list whose entries carry at least a
  display name, with one canonical internal representation for both migrated
  single-author and new multi-author posts. Confirm whether author entries
  need an identifier, URL, or other fields before implementation.
- The request does not specify how multiple authors should appear in the XML
  feed. Decide whether the feed should emit one `<author>` element per author
  in source order or use another approved feed contract.
- Decide whether a post containing both legacy `author` and canonical
  `authors` is accepted during transition, and if so how conflicts are
  detected or resolved. Do not silently define this compatibility behavior
  during implementation.
- The exact point at which legacy rejection is enabled is intentionally
  evidence-driven. The cutover subtask must keep rejection disabled until the
  source and generated-output checks pass and record the evidence used.

## Supporting facts

- `content/posts/first.md` and `content/posts/second.md` currently provide a
  scalar `author` value; `content/posts/posts.json` supplies the post layout
  and `posts` tag.
- `_includes/layouts/post.njk` renders the legacy value directly.
- `content/index.njk`, `content/blog.njk`, and `content/tag-pages.njk` share
  `_includes/postslist.njk`; the current list exposes title and URL only, so
  archive coverage must verify that moving author data does not alter list
  routes, ordering, or rendering.
- `content/feed.xml.njk` reads `post.data.author` directly and is the current
  feed dependency on the legacy field.
- `scripts/new-post.js` accepts `(title, author)` and writes scalar
  `author` front matter.
- `tests/author-output.test.js` and `tests/archive-output.test.js` currently
  contain comments but no decisive assertions. `npm test` runs
  `node --test tests/*.test.js`, while `npm run build` is the production
  Eleventy boundary.
- There is no `docs/index.md`; the maintained documentation currently
  consists of `README.md` and `docs/development/index.md` plus the repository
  guidance in `AGENTS.md`.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

First agree the canonical schema and public feed semantics. Then implement the
normalization/migration boundary, update each production consumer, and update
the authoring helper. Keep the compatibility path active while the integrated
build renders migrated and legacy-shaped fixtures. Finally audit source
references and generated output, record the passing evidence, and only then
enable legacy rejection as a separately reviewable cutover.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- The canonical model must be ordered so author display and feed output are
  deterministic.
- Compatibility should be centralized at the data boundary rather than
  duplicating legacy-field checks across templates.
- The feed contract and dual-field behavior remain open until the requester
  confirms them; they affect public output and validation behavior.
- A source grep alone is not sufficient for cutover: the evidence must include
  a successful production build and inspection/assertions over generated post,
  archive, and feed artifacts.

### Documentation

- Update `README.md` or the owning developer documentation with the canonical
  front-matter example, authoring-helper usage, and the transition/rejection
  status once implementation makes those claims true.
- Do not document legacy rejection as current behavior before the cutover
  evidence gate is complete.
- Keep migration-specific test and verification notes with this task or the
  owning subtask; do not create placeholder documentation sections.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Complete `tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/010-schema-and-content-migration.md`.
- [ ] Complete
      `tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/020-generated-consumers.md`.
- [ ] Complete
      `tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/030-authoring-tool.md`.
- [ ] Complete
      `tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/040-legacy-cutover-evidence.md`.
- [ ] Resolve the public schema and feed/dual-field requirement questions
      before marking execution approved.
- [ ] Keep this plan and child statuses synchronized as execution proceeds.

### Requirement verification

- Canonical metadata and safe source migration: the schema/content subtask
  must show migrated post front matter plus a real Eleventy build that
  renders the migrated posts without route, tag, body, or title loss.
- Generated consumers: the generated-consumers subtask must assert post,
  home/blog/tag archive, and feed artifacts from the production build,
  including ordered multi-author behavior and preserved single-author output.
- Authoring tool: the authoring-tool subtask must test the helper's generated
  front matter through the same parsing/build path used by posts.
- Legacy transition and rejection: the cutover subtask must show no remaining
  legacy source dependencies, successful generated-output assertions, and an
  explicit decision/evidence record before enabling rejection.

### Additional implementation verification

- Run the complete test command and production build after all subtasks are
  integrated.
- Inspect the build output for malformed markup, empty author values, and
  accidental route changes.
- Confirm the repository diff contains only the approved migration,
  verification, and documentation changes.

# Establish the structured author model and migrate posts

Define the canonical post metadata shape, centralize transition handling for
the legacy scalar field, and migrate the checked-in posts without changing
their public identity or content.

Parent Task: tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/000-main.md

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] The canonical field and entry shape are approved and documented in the
      implementation.
- [ ] The model preserves author order and supports current single-author
      posts as well as multiple authors.
- [ ] Existing post front matter is migrated without changing title, body,
      route, tags, or layout behavior.
- [ ] Legacy `author` input remains readable during the transition through one
      defined compatibility boundary.
- [ ] Ambiguous dual-field behavior is resolved and covered before execution
      marks this subtask complete.

## Requirement questions and decisions

- Confirm whether the canonical field is named `authors` and whether entries
  are objects with a required `name`, or whether a different approved shape
  is required.
- Confirm whether author identity/URL fields are in scope now or should remain
  absent until a later migration.
- Confirm the behavior when both `author` and `authors` are present.

## Supporting facts

- Current source files are `content/posts/first.md`,
  `content/posts/second.md`, and the cascade file
  `content/posts/posts.json`.
- Current source values are plain display-name strings, so migration must
  preserve their exact visible names.
- No data migration utility exists in the repository; the checked-in content
  is small enough for a reviewed, explicit source migration once the schema is
  approved.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Add the canonical metadata contract at the narrowest data boundary available
in the Eleventy fixture. During the compatibility window, normalize either
the new field or the approved legacy input into the same ordered author
collection consumed by templates. Migrate both checked-in posts to the new
front-matter shape and add focused fixtures for one and multiple authors.
Preserve the legacy path until the separate cutover task authorizes rejection.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Keep normalization out of individual Nunjucks templates so every consumer
  receives the same ordering and missing-data behavior.
- Do not invent fallback names or silently merge conflicting fields; use the
  approved dual-field policy once the requirement question is answered.
- The source migration is complete only when a production build proves the
  migrated documents still resolve to the same public routes.

### Documentation

- Add the canonical front-matter example to the owning authoring/developer
  documentation as part of this subtask or coordinate that update with the
  authoring-tool subtask.
- Record the compatibility-window status, not final legacy rejection, until
  the cutover evidence passes.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Confirm and record the canonical field/entry schema.
- [ ] Implement the centralized compatibility normalization.
- [ ] Migrate every checked-in post and preserve its existing metadata/body.
- [ ] Add focused one-author and multi-author source fixtures.
- [ ] Run the production build and verify routes/tags/content.

### Requirement verification

- Compare the migrated post metadata and rendered post artifacts against the
  pre-migration title, URL, body, and visible author values.
- Build at least one multi-author fixture and verify the normalized author
  order reaches the rendering boundary.
- Exercise a legacy-shaped fixture while compatibility is enabled to prove
  existing content remains readable.

### Additional implementation verification

- Search all source/templates/scripts for direct legacy-field reads and
  classify each remaining occurrence as compatibility code, test fixture, or
  unresolved dependency.
- Verify no migration step rewrites slugs, dates, tags, or post bodies.

# Move generated pages and feed consumers to structured authors

Update production templates and generated-output coverage so post pages,
shared archive paths, and the XML feed consume the canonical author
representation without breaking existing routes or valid output.

Parent Task: tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/000-main.md
Depends On: tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/010-schema-and-content-migration.md

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] The post layout renders the canonical author data for one and multiple
      authors.
- [ ] Home, blog, and tag archive paths remain on the canonical data path and
      preserve their existing title, URL, ordering, and markup behavior.
- [ ] The feed emits valid, deterministic author output for the approved
      multi-author contract and preserves the current single-author case.
- [ ] Generated-output tests inspect artifacts from a real Eleventy build,
      rather than supplying mocked post data directly to templates.
- [ ] No production consumer depends on the legacy scalar field after the
      compatibility boundary is in place.

## Requirement questions and decisions

- Confirm the public representation of multiple authors in the XML feed
  (recommended default: one `<author>` element per ordered author, if valid
  for the intended feed contract).
- Confirm whether archive lists should display author names during this
  migration or only stop depending on the old field. The current archive list
  displays title and URL only, so adding visible bylines would be a separate
  user-facing change unless approved.

## Supporting facts

- `_includes/layouts/post.njk` currently prints `{{ author }}`.
- `_includes/postslist.njk` is shared by `content/index.njk`,
  `content/blog.njk`, and `content/tag-pages.njk`; it currently prints only
  post links.
- `content/feed.xml.njk` directly prints `post.data.author`.
- `tests/author-output.test.js` and `tests/archive-output.test.js` are not
  currently decisive and need real build assertions.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Adapt the post layout and feed to iterate over the normalized author
collection. Keep the shared archive list's current visible contract unless the
requester approves adding bylines, but make its generated-path coverage prove
that the migration does not bypass or break archive rendering. Extend the
generated-output tests to build the site and inspect post, home, blog, tag,
and feed files for both single- and multi-author cases.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Consumer templates should use normalized data, not independently support
  both legacy and canonical field names.
- Preserve existing archive URLs and order; author display in archives is not
  implied by the migration request because the current list has no byline.
- Treat XML validity and deterministic author ordering as release-blocking
  checks.

### Documentation

- Document the resulting feed/author rendering contract only after the public
  shape is approved and the generated-output assertions pass.
- Keep the archive behavior statement aligned with whether bylines were
  explicitly approved.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Update the post layout to consume normalized structured authors.
- [ ] Update the feed template to the approved multi-author contract.
- [ ] Verify shared archive consumers through home, blog, and tag builds.
- [ ] Replace comment-only output tests with production-build assertions.
- [ ] Confirm no direct legacy reads remain in production templates.

### Requirement verification

- Run `npm run build` with migrated single- and multi-author posts.
- Assert the post HTML contains the expected ordered author output and keeps
  existing post URLs.
- Assert `/index.html`, `/blog/index.html`, and the generated tag page retain
  expected links, order, and valid markup.
- Assert `/feed/feed.xml` contains the approved author elements in source
  order and remains valid XML for both author cardinalities.

### Additional implementation verification

- Check generated output for empty or duplicated author elements.
- Check that the shared archive include is exercised by all three callers,
  not only by the blog page.
- Compare the set of generated routes before and after the migration.

# Update the post-authoring helper for structured authors

Move the new-post helper to the canonical multi-author input and prove that
its output is consumable by the same content/build path as hand-authored
posts.

Parent Task: tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/000-main.md
Depends On: tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/010-schema-and-content-migration.md

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] The helper accepts the approved structured author input, including
      multiple ordered authors.
- [ ] Generated front matter uses the canonical field and valid serialization
      for the repository's parser.
- [ ] The helper no longer requires callers to provide the legacy scalar field
      for new posts.
- [ ] Helper output is verified by parsing/building a representative post,
      not only by comparing a string.
- [ ] Transition guidance makes clear how existing legacy posts and newly
      authored posts differ until cutover.

## Requirement questions and decisions

- Confirm the helper API shape: a list of author objects, a list of display
  names normalized into objects, or another approved interface.
- Confirm whether retaining a compatibility overload for callers of
  `frontMatter(title, author)` is required during the transition. If retained,
  define its warning/deprecation behavior separately from the content parser.

## Supporting facts

- `scripts/new-post.js` currently exports `frontMatter(title, author)` and
  interpolates an unescaped scalar into `author:`.
- There is no existing CLI wrapper or helper test, so the new contract should
  be tested at the exported-function boundary and then through the Eleventy
  build.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Define the helper input in terms of the approved canonical model and serialize
it safely as front matter. Add tests for one and multiple authors, including
names that could expose quoting or YAML serialization problems. Feed the
generated front matter into a temporary or test fixture post and run the real
build path so the helper cannot drift from the content parser.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Prefer structured serialization over hand-built YAML interpolation so author
  names are quoted/escaped correctly.
- Keep any legacy helper overload only if explicitly required; it must not
  cause newly generated content to write the legacy field.
- Do not make the helper reject legacy input before the integrated cutover
  evidence has established that existing content and callers no longer need
  it.

### Documentation

- Update the authoring instructions with the helper signature and a
  canonical one-/multi-author example.
- Explain the compatibility window and the later evidence-gated legacy
  rejection without claiming that rejection has already happened.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Confirm the helper input contract.
- [ ] Serialize canonical author front matter safely.
- [ ] Add one- and multi-author helper tests.
- [ ] Build a post from helper output through the production path.
- [ ] Update the owning authoring documentation.

### Requirement verification

- Assert helper output parses to the approved canonical structure.
- Build representative generated posts and verify author output matches the
  ordered input.
- Exercise any retained legacy call shape and verify its explicitly approved
  transition behavior.

### Additional implementation verification

- Include names containing punctuation, quotes, or non-ASCII characters in
  serialization coverage where the chosen format requires escaping.
- Confirm helper tests do not bypass the front-matter parser or Eleventy
  rendering boundary.

# Gate removal or rejection of the legacy author field

Define and execute the final compatibility gate. Legacy input must remain
available until source and generated-output evidence proves that the migrated
site and authoring path no longer depend on it.

Parent Task: tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/000-main.md
Depends On:
  - tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/010-schema-and-content-migration.md
  - tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/020-generated-consumers.md
  - tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/030-authoring-tool.md

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] The compatibility window remains enabled while migrated and
      legacy-shaped content are both covered.
- [ ] A source/content audit finds no remaining required legacy field usage in
      posts, templates, scripts, or maintained fixtures.
- [ ] A production build proves generated posts, home/blog/tag archives, feed,
      and sitemap still generate successfully from the canonical model.
- [ ] Generated artifacts are inspected/asserted for preserved routes and
      approved author output, including multi-author cases.
- [ ] Legacy rejection/removal is enabled only after the preceding evidence
      passes and is recorded as a deliberate cutover.
- [ ] Post-cutover tests prove the canonical path remains supported and the
      intended legacy failure behavior is explicit.

## Requirement questions and decisions

- Confirm whether the desired final state is hard rejection of legacy
  front matter, removal of a compatibility normalizer, or both.
- Confirm whether any external/untracked content source is in scope for the
  dependency audit; the repository currently exposes only checked-in posts.
- Confirm the exact error/reporting contract for a legacy field after
  rejection. Do not introduce an undocumented failure mode.

## Supporting facts

- Existing generated-output test files are currently placeholders, so the
  cutover cannot rely on prior test names as evidence.
- `npm run build` is the production generation boundary and `npm test` is the
  repository test boundary.
- Direct legacy dependencies are currently visible in the post layout, feed,
  and authoring helper; archive rendering must still be checked because it is
  a shared production path even though it does not currently print authors.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Keep compatibility enabled while all child changes land. Run a repository-wide
dependency audit and the complete production build/test suite with migrated
single- and multi-author content. Inspect the generated artifact set and
assert the relevant public output. Record the evidence and approval decision.
Only then make the legacy field rejectable/removable, update the tests and
guidance for that final state, and rerun the same production checks to prove
the cutover did not regress generated pages.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- The cutover is a separate compatibility state, not an incidental cleanup
  bundled into the first source migration.
- A passing source search is necessary but not sufficient; generated-output
  evidence is mandatory because Eleventy data cascade and template behavior
  can retain dependencies not obvious from migrated front matter.
- If the evidence finds an unresolved dependency, leave compatibility enabled,
  record the dependency, and do not reject the legacy field.

### Documentation

- Record the final compatibility state and migration evidence in the owning
  developer documentation.
- If rejection is not yet safe, document the remaining dependency and keep the
  legacy format described as transitional rather than unsupported.
- Do not rewrite historical generated output by hand; update its maintained
  source and regenerate it through Eleventy.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Keep legacy compatibility active during integrated verification.
- [ ] Audit content, templates, scripts, tests, and documentation for legacy
      dependencies.
- [ ] Run `npm test` and `npm run build` with representative content.
- [ ] Inspect/assert generated post, archive, feed, and sitemap artifacts.
- [ ] Record the evidence and obtain the cutover decision.
- [ ] If approved, enable explicit legacy rejection/removal.
- [ ] Rerun all decisive checks after cutover and update documentation.

### Requirement verification

- Source evidence: repository-wide search plus inspection of every remaining
  match, with no unclassified required legacy dependency.
- Generated evidence: successful production build and assertions over all
  public artifact classes named in the requirements.
- Compatibility evidence: a legacy-shaped fixture passes before cutover;
  after cutover, the canonical fixture passes and the approved legacy failure
  behavior is asserted.
- Preservation evidence: generated route set, archive links/order, post
  content, feed author order, and sitemap URLs remain valid.

### Additional implementation verification

- Run the complete test suite after any rejection change, not only the
  focused author tests.
- Check for stale generated files or documentation that still teaches the
  rejected format.
- Keep the evidence record in this task's completion notes so a later
  maintainer can distinguish “not found” from “not searched.”

# Migrate post author metadata to a structured multi-author form

Plan the staged migration from the post front matter `author` string to a
structured multi-author contract across source content, authoring tools,
templates, archives, feeds, and the legacy-field cutover.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] Define and adopt one canonical structured multi-author representation for
  post metadata.
- [ ] Keep existing legacy-author content buildable and renderable during the
  migration transition, without breaking existing generated pages or feeds.
- [ ] Move post templates, archive/list paths, and feed generation to consume
  the canonical author representation.
- [ ] Update the post authoring helper to emit the canonical representation and
  support the approved multi-author input.
- [ ] Migrate every existing post safely, preserving its current author data and
  preventing dropped, duplicated, or reordered authors.
- [ ] Reject the legacy single-name form only after content inventory and
  generated-output evidence show that no supported source or output path still
  depends on it.
- [ ] Record the current authoring contract and the completed cutover in the
  maintained documentation, without documenting target behavior as current
  before implementation is complete.

## Unresolved requirement questions and decisions

- **Requirement question — canonical schema:** What is the exact field name and
  element shape? For example, should the field be an array of display-name
  strings or an array of author objects with stable identifiers and names?
  This changes front matter, the authoring helper API, and every renderer.
- **Requirement question — rendered form:** How should one and multiple authors
  appear on post pages, archive/list views, and the feed? The migration should
  preserve the current one-name presentation where applicable, but the
  separator, ordering, and feed serialization for multiple authors need
  approval.
- **Requirement question — compatibility boundary:** During transition, should
  legacy `author` be normalized in Eleventy data, accepted only by the
  authoring tool, or accepted by both? The final rejection point and its error
  message should be explicit before implementation.
- **Decision:** Use separate source migration, output migration, and
  evidence-gated rejection boundaries. No rejection should be enabled merely
  because the new field exists.
- **Decision:** Do not add author identity pages, profile URLs, or a new
  persistent author registry unless the schema decision explicitly requires
  them.

## Scope and workstreams

The work is decomposed into three dependent subtasks:

1. Establish the source contract, authoring-tool behavior, and migrated post
   content.
2. Convert every production output surface that consumes or exposes author
   metadata.
3. Prove that the legacy form is unused, then enable its rejection and record
   the final supported contract.

This planning task does not modify application code, content, generated
output, tests, or maintained documentation.

## Research and supporting facts

- The two existing post sources,
  `content/posts/first.md` and `content/posts/second.md`, use quoted scalar
  `author` values.
- `scripts/new-post.js` emits the legacy `author` front matter and accepts one
  author argument.
- `_includes/layouts/post.njk` renders `author` directly.
- `content/feed.xml.njk` reads `post.data.author` directly.
- The home page, blog archive, and tag pages all use
  `_includes/postslist.njk`; that shared list currently renders only title and
  URL, so its author behavior must be reviewed as the archive integration
  point even though it has no direct legacy-field reference today.
- `content/posts/posts.json` supplies the shared post layout and `posts` tag;
  there is no separate author data collection or author registry.
- `tests/author-output.test.js` and `tests/archive-output.test.js` contain
  comments describing intended coverage but no assertions, so they are not
  evidence for the migration or the cutover gate.
- The repository has no authoring or front matter guide beyond the general
  `README.md`; documentation should remain small and owned by the site
  package.

## Subtasks

- [ ] [tasks/20260920-author-metadata-migration/010-source-contract-and-content-migration.md](tasks/20260920-author-metadata-migration/010-source-contract-and-content-migration.md)
- [ ] [tasks/20260920-author-metadata-migration/020-rendering-and-output-surfaces.md](tasks/20260920-author-metadata-migration/020-rendering-and-output-surfaces.md)
- [ ] [tasks/20260920-author-metadata-migration/030-cutover-evidence-and-legacy-rejection.md](tasks/20260920-author-metadata-migration/030-cutover-evidence-and-legacy-rejection.md)

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Execute the subtasks in numeric order after the unresolved schema,
presentation, and compatibility questions are approved. Keep the old input
readable until the final evidence gate; the new field must be exercised through
the actual Eleventy build rather than through isolated template mocks.

The first workstream establishes the canonical source representation,
normalizes legacy input for the transition if that is the approved boundary,
updates `scripts/new-post.js`, and migrates every existing post. The second
workstream updates the post layout, shared archive/list path, and feed to use
the canonical data while preserving the established output for the existing
single-author posts. It also adds coverage for multiple authors and for all
archive entry points. The last workstream inventories source references,
builds the site, inspects generated post/archive/feed output, and only then
enables a clear failure for remaining legacy input.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- The staged compatibility decision is approved for planning: migration and
  rendering must be independently verifiable before legacy rejection.
- The exact field/schema, multi-author display/serialization, and enforcement
  boundary remain open requirement questions. Resolve them before changing the
  requirements checklist or marking execution approved.
- The final rejection must be exercised through the real authoring/build path;
  a test that bypasses front matter parsing or supplies already-normalized
  data is not decisive.

### Documentation

Update `README.md` or the smallest more appropriate package-owned guide with
the canonical front matter example, authoring-tool input, transition status,
and final rejection behavior. Do not describe legacy rejection as current
until the evidence gate passes. No new documentation directory or placeholder
page is needed.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Resolve the canonical schema, presentation, and compatibility-boundary
  questions.
- [ ] Approve this plan and mark it `Approved` before execution.
- [ ] Complete
  `010-source-contract-and-content-migration.md`.
- [ ] Complete `020-rendering-and-output-surfaces.md` against the production
  build.
- [ ] Complete `030-cutover-evidence-and-legacy-rejection.md`.
- [ ] Update maintained authoring documentation after the supported behavior is
  true.
- [ ] Record implementation and completion notes with evidence in this task
  file and its subtasks.

### Requirement verification

- **Canonical representation and authoring tool:** Verify the approved field
  shape in every migrated post, invoke the real `scripts/new-post.js` export
  with one and multiple authors, and parse the resulting front matter through
  the normal Eleventy input path.
- **Transition compatibility:** Build with a representative legacy fixture
  before the final cutover and assert that the post page and feed still
  contain the same author information and valid output.
- **Output migration:** Run the production build and inspect a post page, home
  page, blog archive, tag archive, and feed. Assert that each author-bearing
  surface is derived from canonical data and that multiple authors are
  complete, ordered, and serialized according to the approved contract.
- **Existing-content migration:** Inventory all post front matter, compare the
  pre-migration author values with the canonical values, and build the full
  site to catch malformed metadata.
- **Legacy rejection gate:** Require both a repository/content scan with no
  supported legacy inputs and generated-output checks showing no legacy data
  path remains before asserting that legacy input fails. Keep a focused
  negative test for the final rejection.
- **Documentation:** Review the maintained guide against the behavior proven
  by the final build and tests.

# Establish the structured author contract and migrate source content

Define the canonical post metadata shape, move the authoring helper to that
shape, and migrate existing post front matter while preserving all author
information during the compatibility window.

Parent Task: tasks/20260920-author-metadata-migration/000-main.md

Depends On: None

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] The approved structured multi-author schema is documented as the
  canonical post input contract.
- [ ] `scripts/new-post.js` accepts the approved multi-author input and emits
  valid canonical front matter for one and multiple authors.
- [ ] Every existing post is migrated without losing, duplicating, or
  reordering author data.
- [ ] Legacy source data remains normalizable or otherwise supported at the
  approved transition boundary until the cutover subtask supplies its evidence.

## Unresolved requirement questions and decisions

- The parent task's canonical field name, element shape, and authoring-helper
  API must be resolved before execution; this subtask must not invent them.
- The transition behavior for a legacy scalar is a parent-level compatibility
  decision. If normalization is selected, define whether it produces a
  one-element canonical list and where that normalization occurs.

## Research and supporting facts

- `content/posts/first.md` contains the author value `Ada Example`.
- `content/posts/second.md` contains the author value `Grace Example`.
- `scripts/new-post.js` currently has the signature
  `frontMatter(title, author)` and writes `author: "..."`.
- `content/posts/posts.json` does not define or transform author metadata, so
  the source contract cannot currently be delegated to a collection data
  file.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

After the parent questions are approved, define the canonical representation
and the compatibility normalization boundary. Update the authoring helper to
produce that representation for one and multiple authors, including safe
quoting/escaping for names. Migrate the two existing post files and any
additional post files discovered by the content inventory. Preserve author
order and compare the old scalar values with the migrated one-author values.

Add focused source-level evidence for the helper output and content inventory,
but leave final acceptance of rendered pages and the legacy rejection to the
dependent subtasks. If the chosen transition strategy needs Eleventy data
normalization or validation, keep that logic at the agreed source/build
boundary and document its lifetime so it can be removed or disabled at
cutover.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Keep the migration lossless: existing one-author values become exactly one
  canonical author entry, with no implicit author identity or link creation.
- Resolve any escaping or malformed-input behavior as part of the approved
  front matter contract; do not silently invent fallback authors.
- The compatibility adapter, if used, must be exercised with an actual legacy
  post and must remain available until subtask 030 closes the evidence gate.

### Documentation

Provide the canonical front matter and authoring-helper examples to the
parent's package documentation plan. Do not publish the legacy rejection rule
from this subtask while the output and content evidence is incomplete.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Confirm the approved canonical schema and helper API.
- [ ] Define and implement the transition normalization/validation boundary.
- [ ] Update the authoring helper for one and multiple authors.
- [ ] Inventory and migrate all existing post front matter.
- [ ] Add focused source/content evidence and pass it through the normal
  parsing boundary.
- [ ] Update this subtask with implementation and completion notes after
  execution.

### Requirement verification

- **Canonical source contract:** Parse generated helper output and each
  migrated post through the actual Eleventy input path; assert the canonical
  field and exact author list.
- **Authoring tool:** Exercise one-author and multiple-author calls,
  including names requiring front matter quoting/escaping, and assert valid
  output without relying on a hand-constructed fixture.
- **Lossless migration:** Compare the complete pre-migration author inventory
  with the canonical post inventory, including count and order.
- **Transition support:** Build or parse a real legacy-form fixture at the
  selected compatibility boundary and verify it normalizes to the same data
  as its migrated equivalent.

# Move author rendering across pages, archives, and feeds

Convert the production templates and all archive/list entry points to consume
the structured author collection, while preserving generated output for
existing one-author posts and defining deterministic multi-author output.

Parent Task: tasks/20260920-author-metadata-migration/000-main.md

Depends On: tasks/20260920-author-metadata-migration/010-source-contract-and-content-migration.md

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] The post layout renders authors from the canonical structured field.
- [ ] The shared archive/list path and its home, blog, and tag-page consumers no
  longer depend on the legacy field when author data is rendered or exposed.
- [ ] The feed renders the canonical author data according to the approved
  feed representation.
- [ ] Legacy-form input remains renderable during the approved transition
  window, if the parent compatibility decision requires it.
- [ ] One-author output remains compatible with the current generated pages,
  while multiple authors are complete and deterministic.

## Unresolved requirement questions and decisions

- The parent task must approve the visible multi-author formatting and the
  feed serialization before this subtask can define exact assertions.
- The current archive list renders only titles and URLs. Confirm whether the
  migration should add an author byline there or only ensure that any existing
  or newly exposed archive author data uses the canonical field.
- Decide whether the feed emits one author element per author or one
  serialized element, and preserve the existing feed contract for a
  one-author post unless the approved migration explicitly changes it.

## Research and supporting facts

- `_includes/layouts/post.njk` currently prints `{{ author }}`.
- `content/feed.xml.njk` currently prints `post.data.author` inside each
  entry.
- `content/index.njk`, `content/blog.njk`, and `content/tag-pages.njk` all
  include `_includes/postslist.njk`.
- `_includes/postslist.njk` currently prints only `post.data.title` and
  `post.url`; it is the shared integration point for all three archive paths.
- `tests/author-output.test.js` and `tests/archive-output.test.js` do not
  currently run a build or assert generated output.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Using the canonical field from subtask 010, update the post layout, shared
archive/list rendering, and feed template. Keep compatibility handling at the
approved boundary so templates do not each implement divergent legacy
fallbacks. If archive bylines are part of the approved output, render them
through one shared author formatter and exercise home, blog, and tag pages.
If archives intentionally remain title-only, verify they do not read the
legacy field and add coverage that the shared path remains safe with canonical
data.

Replace the placeholder tests with production-build assertions. Build the
site using the normal Eleventy command, then inspect representative generated
post, home, blog, tag, and feed files. Include a multi-author fixture or
migrated post so the tests prove list completeness, ordering, escaping, and
feed validity rather than only checking that files exist.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Centralize any presentation logic needed by several templates so post,
  archive, and feed output cannot drift.
- Do not remove transition support from templates until subtask 030 has
  completed its source and generated-output evidence gate.
- Resolve archive byline behavior and feed element shape before fixing exact
  output assertions.

### Documentation

Supply the final visible/output examples and feed behavior to the parent
documentation update. Do not document unverified generated output as a
supported contract.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Confirm archive presentation and feed serialization.
- [ ] Update the post layout to consume canonical authors.
- [ ] Update the shared archive/list integration and all archive consumers as
  required by the approved output contract.
- [ ] Update the feed to consume canonical authors.
- [ ] Replace placeholder author/archive tests with production-build checks.
- [ ] Verify legacy-form rendering during the transition.
- [ ] Update this subtask with implementation and completion notes after
  execution.

### Requirement verification

- **Post rendering:** Run the real build and assert the generated post page
  contains the approved one- and multiple-author representation.
- **Archive paths:** Inspect generated home, blog archive, and tag archive
  pages and assert the shared list path is compatible with canonical author
  data and has no legacy-field dependency.
- **Feed:** Inspect the generated feed XML and assert every author is present,
  ordered, escaped, and serialized according to the approved contract.
- **Transition:** Build with a real legacy-form post before cutover and
  compare its author output with the equivalent canonical post.
- **Regression:** Confirm existing titles, URLs, post bodies, and one-author
  author output remain intact in the generated files.

# Prove migration completeness and reject the legacy author form

Own the final compatibility gate: establish that source content and generated
outputs no longer depend on the single-name field, then enable and verify
legacy-form rejection.

Parent Task: tasks/20260920-author-metadata-migration/000-main.md

Depends On:
tasks/20260920-author-metadata-migration/010-source-contract-and-content-migration.md
tasks/20260920-author-metadata-migration/020-rendering-and-output-surfaces.md

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] A complete content/source inventory shows no supported post still relies
  on the legacy single-name field.
- [ ] A clean production build and generated-output inspection show that post
  pages, home/blog/tag archives, and feeds do not depend on the legacy field.
- [ ] Transition compatibility is retained until both evidence conditions pass.
- [ ] After the evidence gate passes, the approved boundary rejects legacy
  input with a clear actionable error.
- [ ] The final documentation describes only the now-supported canonical form
  and the verified rejection behavior.

## Unresolved requirement questions and decisions

- The exact enforcement boundary remains the parent-level requirement
  question: authoring helper, front matter validation, Eleventy build, or a
  combination. The chosen boundary must cover all supported authoring paths.
- Decide whether a legacy-field negative test remains permanently as regression
  coverage after rejection; the recommended approach is yes, because it
  protects the compatibility contract.

## Research and supporting facts

- The repository currently has two post files and both use `author`; the
  content inventory must be rerun after migration rather than assuming this
  remains the complete set.
- Existing generated-output tests are placeholders, so current test names
  cannot serve as the evidence gate.
- The build output directory is `_site`, and the normal build command is
  `npm run build`.
- The legacy field is currently consumed directly by the post layout and feed;
  any remaining reference or fallback must be classified as intentional
  transition code before rejection.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

First run a repository/content inventory that distinguishes migrated source,
intentional compatibility code, tests, documentation, and generated output.
Then run the production build with representative migrated and
multiple-author content and inspect all author-bearing output surfaces from
subtask 020. Repeat with a real legacy fixture while compatibility is still
enabled. Record the commands and decisive assertions in the implementation
notes so the cutover is auditable.

Only when the inventory and generated-output checks are both clean, enable the
approved legacy rejection at the agreed boundary. Add a negative test that
passes legacy input through the actual supported path and asserts the clear
failure. Remove obsolete compatibility branches only after that test and the
full production build pass; retain intentional historical migration evidence
as documentation or test data without allowing it as supported input.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- The rejection gate is a hard dependency, not a cleanup step: no legacy
  rejection may ship on source inspection alone.
- Generated-output evidence must cross the Eleventy build boundary and include
  the public page/archive/feed paths, not just inspect template source.
- Resolve the enforcement boundary before execution and do not broaden it to
  reject unrelated unknown metadata.

### Documentation

Update the package-owned authoring guidance only after the gate passes. State
the canonical field, accepted multi-author shape, authoring-helper usage, and
the legacy-field rejection with an example of the supported replacement. If
the project retains migration notes, label them as historical rather than
supported input instructions.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Confirm the enforcement boundary and permanent negative-test policy.
- [ ] Inventory source/content and classify every remaining legacy reference.
- [ ] Run clean production-build and generated-output evidence.
- [ ] Verify transition compatibility before rejection.
- [ ] Enable legacy rejection only after both evidence conditions pass.
- [ ] Run the negative legacy-input test through the real supported path.
- [ ] Run the full test suite and final production build.
- [ ] Update maintained documentation and record immutable completion notes.

### Requirement verification

- **Content evidence:** Search all supported post sources and authoring
  inputs, then parse the complete inventory through the normal build path.
  The only remaining legacy references may be explicitly classified
  migration fixtures or historical documentation.
- **Generated-output evidence:** Build from migrated content and inspect
  generated post, home, blog, tag, and feed files for complete canonical
  author output and absence of legacy-dependent rendering.
- **Transition ordering:** Demonstrate that the legacy fixture succeeds before
  the gate and fails only after the clean inventory/build evidence is
  recorded.
- **Rejection:** Invoke the actual supported input/build path with a legacy
  `author` field and assert a deterministic, actionable failure.
- **Final regression:** Run `npm test` and `npm run build`, then verify the
  generated pages and feed remain complete after compatibility code is
  removed or disabled.

# Migrate post author metadata

Plan the migration from the single `author` front-matter value to a canonical
ordered multi-author value while keeping legacy content and generated output
working until repository evidence permits the legacy form to be rejected.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] R1. Define and adopt one canonical structured author collection that
  supports one or more authors, preserves source order, and exposes each
  author's display identity to every production consumer.
- [ ] R2. Preserve existing content and generated pages during the transition:
  legacy `author` content must continue to normalize to the canonical model
  until the retirement gate passes, without changing post bodies, routes,
  tags, archive membership, feed location, or sitemap coverage.
- [ ] R3. Move the authoring helper to the canonical model and make its
  single- and multi-author behavior explicit, while preserving safe input
  compatibility during the transition.
- [ ] R4. Migrate every repository post from the legacy field without losing,
  duplicating, or reordering author names, and leave auditable source evidence
  that the migration is complete.
- [ ] R5. Move post layouts, home/blog/tag archive consumers, shared post-list
  rendering, feeds, and any other author consumers to the canonical model.
  Generated pages must continue to build and all authors must be represented
  deterministically.
- [ ] R6. Reject the legacy field only after both source/consumer evidence and
  production generated-output evidence show that nothing in the repository
  still depends on it; the rejection must have a clear diagnostic and a
  regression check.
- [ ] R7. Update maintained authoring documentation and regression evidence
  with the supported canonical form and the completed transition state.

## Scope and workstreams

The scope is the repository’s Eleventy source, content, authoring helper,
production templates, build-time validation, tests, and the maintained
documentation that explains how posts are authored. Existing URLs, post body
content, tags, archive membership, feed location, and sitemap behavior are
compatibility constraints.

The work is intentionally divided by independently reviewable capability:

- establish the data contract and authoring boundary;
- migrate all rendering and collection consumers;
- migrate source content and prove its inventory is clean; and
- perform the generated-output/content gate before enforcing canonical-only
  input.

Author profile pages, stable author IDs, roles, avatars, author sorting, and
new public routes are out of scope unless the canonical-shape decision below
requires one of them.

## Subtasks

- [ ] tasks/20260920-author-metadata-migration/010-author-contract-and-authoring.md
- [ ] tasks/20260920-author-metadata-migration/020-rendering-and-archive-consumers.md
- [ ] tasks/20260920-author-metadata-migration/030-source-content-migration.md
- [ ] tasks/20260920-author-metadata-migration/040-output-evidence-and-legacy-retirement.md

## Unresolved requirement questions and decisions

- Requirement question: does “structured” mean an ordered list of display
  strings (`authors: ["Ada Example"]`) or an ordered list of records with a
  required `name` (`authors: [{ name: "Ada Example" }]`)? Recommendation:
  use records with a required `name` and no additional fields in this
  migration, so each author has an explicit structured boundary without
  inventing profile behavior.
- Requirement question: if both `author` and `authors` are present during the
  compatibility window, should the build fail as ambiguous input or should
  one field win? Recommendation: fail with a targeted diagnostic; silently
  choosing one would hide a content migration error.
- Design decision: install compatibility normalization before changing
  consumers or source content; migrate content and collect output evidence;
  only then enable canonical-only rejection. This ordering is required by the
  requested transition guarantee.
- Recommendation requiring confirmation at execution time: preserve the
  existing one-author display text, join multiple post-page names in source
  order with a deterministic separator, and emit one feed author element per
  canonical author. This avoids a URL or feed-location redesign while making
  multiple authors lossless.

## Research and supporting facts

- `content/posts/first.md` and `content/posts/second.md` are the only current
  posts and each has a scalar quoted `author`.
- `_includes/layouts/post.njk` renders `author` directly.
- `content/feed.xml.njk` reads `post.data.author` directly and currently emits
  one author element per post.
- `content/index.njk`, `content/blog.njk`, and `content/tag-pages.njk` all
  use `_includes/postslist.njk`; that include currently renders titles and
  links but no author data. These archive paths still need an explicit
  canonical-model audit and route/output checks.
- `content/posts/posts.json` supplies the shared post layout and `posts` tag;
  `content/sitemap.xml.njk` enumerates all page URLs but has no author lookup.

  the legacy field.

  contain comments only, so there is no executable author or archive
  regression evidence to preserve.

  installed in this planning checkout, so neither command is evidence for
  this Draft plan.

  no archive pagination specification exists. The smallest likely maintained
  documentation change is a focused authoring section in `README.md`, unless

single normalization/validation boundary that can represent canonical input

convert every existing post, run a scoped source/consumer inventory, and
exercise a real Eleventy build that checks post pages, archive routes, feed
entries, and sitemap coverage. The final subtask removes the compatibility
path and enables a canonical-only rejection only after those checks pass.

Each child owns its focused tests and documentation updates; the final child
owns the cross-capability retirement gate rather than being a generic test
or cleanup task.

- Normalization should live at the Eleventy data boundary so layouts and

- The legacy adapter must be observable in tests and removable without
  changing canonical rendering.
- The final rejection is planned as a build-time validation failure with a

- Keep migration-only rationale and evidence in these task files rather than

  the gate, while canonical one/multiple-author input remains accepted.
- [ ] Run the full available test/build commands and record blocked commands
  or environment limitations instead of treating them as passing.

## Research and supporting facts

- The repository currently has no executable generated-output assertions;
  both relevant test files are comment-only placeholders.
- `npm run build` invokes Eleventy and writes `_site`; `npm test` runs the

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Add or complete the generated-output test harness so it invokes the real
Eleventy build and inspects `_site`, rather than supplying mocked post data.
Before retirement, run a scoped inventory over production content, templates,
configuration, scripts, and tests; allow only the explicitly documented

front-matter field. Re-run the canonical build and all tests after that

weakening the normal build path or leaving a legacy fixture in the production

- Define the audit scope so historical task text or a deliberate negative

### Documentation

producer_records.response:
Task structure is created — only `tasks/` was added, nothing else touched. Here's the plan for approval.

## Structure created

`tasks/20260920-notes-query-capability/` — one main task plus three subtasks, decomposed along the three independently maintained compatibility boundaries (per `AGENTS.md` project context), not by files or test levels:

- **`000-main.md`** — requirements checklist (R1–R7), decision register, cross-boundary plan, requirement→evidence mapping
- **`010-service-query-api.md`** — the capability on `GET /notes/` + the contract specification; no dependencies (contract-first)
- **`020-client-query-support.md`** — `NotesClient.list_notes()` optional params; depends on 010
- **`030-cli-query-command.md`** — `notes list` flags; depends on 010 and 020

The dependency declarations make any other execution order unsafe — that's how "contract stable before consumers rely on it" is enforced structurally, and why the CLI's production-path test must run the real package from 020.

## Approach

Freeze one HTTP contract, implement it once per boundary in order 010 → 020 → 030, with evidence crossing each boundary's real public path. Key finding from inspection: client and CLI tests currently only cross fakes — nothing proves the production chain today, which is exactly what 030's decisive test closes (installed console script → `from_environment()` → real httpx → real running service, no injected client).

## Material decisions (recommended, need your approval)

1. Extend the existing `GET /notes/` route with optional params rather than a new endpoint
2. `limit`/`offset` with server-enforced `LIMIT_MAX` (100) rather than cursors
3. Out-of-range values → `422`, not silent clamping
4. **Bounded-vs-preserved resolution**: bounds apply only when `limit` is supplied; absent `limit` still returns every note — a default page size would silently truncate the collection for existing consumers
5. Deterministic ordering (`<field> <dir>, id ASC` tiebreaker) guaranteed for any parameterized query; the unparameterized request keeps today's exact behavior with no new ordering guarantee
6. `q` = case-insensitive substring over `title`/`description` (SQLite `LIKE` is ASCII-only — documented, not hidden)
7. One-to-one naming across all three boundaries (`limit/offset/sort/order/q` / `--limit --offset --sort --order --q`)
8. Bare JSON array response retained (no envelope → no total count; recorded consequence)
9. `notes-client` and `notes-cli` bump to `0.2.0` in the same change

No requirement questions are open — the request fixes the outcomes; the decisions above choose within them.

## Acceptance evidence

Service: integration tests over the public route (bounds rejection, tie-collision sort stability, filter semantics, unparameterized equivalence). Client: request-mapping component tests + one real-HTTP integration test. CLI: parser unit tests + the production-path run. Existing tests at all three boundaries stay green unchanged.

## Documentation

Spec at `docs/notes-query.md` (service owns the HTTP contract; `docs/development/index.md` currently records its absence) plus root/client/CLI READMEs, each landing in the same change as the behavior it describes.

## Risks

Shared `./notes.db` across service tests (mitigate with unique seeded data); ASCII-only case-folding must be documented, not silently promised; spec/implementation drift guarded by tests pinning the documented values.

## Exclusions

No schema changes, auth, cursors, envelopes, new subcommands/endpoints, or unreachable-service error behavior (unspecified today, not invented). Nothing implemented — plan is `Status: Draft`.

Execution waits for your approval. If you adjust any decision, I'll revise the affected subtask files and the plan returns to Draft.
